Azyz6klPCa.one_liner: Microbiome foundation model using relation-biased self-attention over four taxonomic ranks with multiscale compositional reconstruction.
Azyz6klPCa.problem: Existing gut microbiome foundation models use flat taxon representations and cannot exploit known taxonomic hierarchies.
Azyz6klPCa.method: TaxoMFM jointly models four taxonomic ranks (species, genus, family, order), encodes taxonomy through relation-biased self-attention, and trains with multiscale compositional reconstruction and hierarchical composition learning using a hierarchical compositional decoder. The authors also build TaxoGut-HPP, 100,806 gut microbiome profiles from 231 source cohorts.
Azyz6klPCa.key_idea: Inject taxonomy into self-attention as a relation bias across four ranks, and reconstruct composition at each rank with a hierarchical decoder.
Azyz6klPCa.evidence: TaxoGut-HPP covers 40 classification and eight regression tasks (disease, gut health, host trait, liver ultrasound phenotype), plus cross-cohort zero-shot transfer and analyses of robustness to database updates and species-vocabulary shifts.
Azyz6klPCa.claimed_gains: Cross-cohort zero-shot AUROCs of 0.838 for colorectal cancer, 0.736 for type 2 diabetes, and 0.722 for inflammatory bowel disease, with the strongest overall performance across phenotype tasks.

jHeJyv15lH.one_liner: Finite-sample high-probability last-iterate analysis of synchronous tabular quantile TD via a global-to-local, variance-drift matching argument.
jHeJyv15lH.problem: Quantile TD's finite-time behavior is poorly understood because its update is nonlinear and nonsmooth, and the stability needed for a sharp rate holds only near the target.
jHeJyv15lH.method: Proves a global high-probability last-iterate guarantee for synchronous tabular QTD under general positive, nonincreasing step sizes and arbitrary initialization in the natural parameter range. The proof first uses Bellman contraction and CDF monotonicity to get near the target, then a variance-drift matching argument and local contraction sharpen the error.
jHeJyv15lH.key_idea: Two-stage global-to-local proof: Bellman contraction and CDF monotonicity reach a neighborhood, then variance-drift matching controls accumulated noise for sharp local rates.
jHeJyv15lH.evidence: Theoretical analysis only, as stated in the abstract; no experiments are mentioned.
jHeJyv15lH.claimed_gains: For step-size exponent a in (0,1) the last iterate converges at rate T^(-a/2) in infinity norm, a tuned harmonic schedule recovers T^(-1/2), and the infinity-Wasserstein error scales as sqrt(m/T), all up to logarithmic factors.

gnC09U8SIF.one_liner: Unsupervised cross-modal hashing using cascaded high-order interaction blocks and relational distillation from a fused teacher to unimodal encoders.
gnC09U8SIF.problem: Unsupervised cross-modal hashing must exploit image-text interactions during training yet transfer that multimodal knowledge to independently deployable unimodal hash encoders.
gnC09U8SIF.method: HOCH stacks cascaded multi-head interaction blocks that form products of normalized low-rank projections and update image and text representations through gated residuals. An adaptive modality fusion module builds a multimodal teacher, and modality-specific relational distillation transfers cross-modal and intra-modal similarity structure to the image and text hash branches.
gnC09U8SIF.key_idea: Progressive low-rank product interactions between modalities feed a fused teacher whose similarity structure is distilled into separate image and text hash encoders.
gnC09U8SIF.evidence: Experiments on MIRFlickr, NUS-WIDE and MSCOCO with hash-code lengths from 16 to 128 bits.
gnC09U8SIF.claimed_gains: Reported as achieving the best results on MIRFlickr, NUS-WIDE and MSCOCO at 16 to 128 bits; the abstract is cut off before any numbers.

e3DQlvGOYa.one_liner: Mean-field ODE theory for multi-component online ICA predicts decoupled and competition regimes and learnability boundaries.
e3DQlvGOYa.problem: High-dimensional theory of ICA is largely limited to single-component recovery and does not describe the coupling induced by simultaneous learning and orthogonalization.
e3DQlvGOYa.method: They derive an asymptotically exact mean-field theory for multi-component online ICA in which the joint empirical distribution of estimates and true components converges to a deterministic process, giving a closed ODE system for the overlap matrix. Steady-state analysis yields explicit learnability boundaries linking step size, data moments and initialization.
e3DQlvGOYa.key_idea: In the high-dimensional limit, track the overlap matrix between learned and true components with a closed ODE system that captures orthogonalization-induced coupling.
e3DQlvGOYa.evidence: Asymptotic theory with steady-state analysis, checked in experiments on synthetic data and a second setting that is cut off in the abstract.
e3DQlvGOYa.claimed_gains: not stated; theoretical predictions include a staircase in the number of recoverable components as the learning rate changes.

inz4OAiTAa.one_liner: Music-to-dance generation where a choreographic world model picks which motions to retrieve and when to inject them.
inz4OAiTAa.problem: Existing retrieval-augmented dance methods use motion memory poorly because of how sparse references are allocated in time and because refinement depends sequentially on an initial draft.
inz4OAiTAa.method: The Anticipate-Attribute-Anchor (3A) module proposes motion hypotheses from musical transitions, selects reference moments by explanatory gain (reduction in prediction error), and retrieves real motions as anchors. Music-driven retrieval runs in parallel with flow sampling, Mid-Flow Anchor Inpainting merges the references into the same generation pass, and a part-aware generator with local-to-global flow supervision supports natural transitions.
inz4OAiTAa.key_idea: Select reference moments by explanatory gain (prediction-error reduction) and inpaint retrieved motion anchors mid-flow within a single sampling pass.
inz4OAiTAa.evidence: Experiments on FineDance and AIST++, a user study, and systematic ablations.
inz4OAiTAa.claimed_gains: Claims the best-reported dance generation performance on FineDance and AIST++; no numbers are stated.

txswzldKOg.one_liner: Benchmark and training-free agentic framework for inferring user-level private attributes by connecting clues across multimodal social media posts.
txswzldKOg.problem: Harmless-looking details in single posts can jointly expose a user's home, workplace, or routine, but no shared benchmark or severity-aware metric exists for user-level multimodal privacy leakage.
txswzldKOg.method: SopriBench groups synthetic posts by user with ground-truth private attributes and post-level evidence, scored by a Privacy Exposure Score (PES) that weighs specificity and sensitivity. Argus is a training-free agent that tracks possible attribute values, verifies supporting evidence, and assembles user-level privacy profiles.
txswzldKOg.key_idea: Track candidate attribute values across posts and verify each with supporting evidence before assembling a user-level privacy profile.
txswzldKOg.evidence: SopriBench has 50 user profiles, 500 posts, and 1,569 images; a study with 11 users verifying inferences about themselves and an ablation on verification are also reported.
txswzldKOg.claimed_gains: Argus achieves a 25% relative PES gain over the strongest baseline, SingleAgent, and 75.5% precision versus 51.4% for SingleAgent in the 11-user study.

C7gKNd4S4R.one_liner: Higher-order graph learning where latent group factors define energies that drive node-state evolution for brain network analysis.
C7gKNd4S4R.problem: Higher-order graph models use group structure only as a predefined aggregation pattern, and physics-inspired energy models rely on node-wise or pairwise interactions on fixed graphs.
C7gKNd4S4R.method: HOPE infers instance-specific latent factors with sparse soft memberships and converts their group-wise interactions into factor-wise energies that govern node-state evolution. It alternates factor inference with structure-aware gradient-flow updates, with each fixed-factor evolution following dissipative continuous-time dynamics.
C7gKNd4S4R.key_idea: Alternate inferring sparse soft-membership latent factors with gradient-flow updates on factor-wise energies, so higher-order structure and node states co-evolve.
C7gKNd4S4R.evidence: Experiments on diverse brain networks covering neurodegenerative and neurodevelopmental disorders, with learned factors and energies used to identify disease-relevant ROI groups.
C7gKNd4S4R.claimed_gains: Consistently improves disease prediction across neurodegenerative and neurodevelopmental disorders (no numbers stated).

XvblPIlleK.one_liner: Smooths regularized l_p regression with p-Huber approximations and accelerated proximal gradient to reach optimal matrix-vector complexity for 1<p<2.
XvblPIlleK.problem: For regularized l_p regression with p in (1,2), the universal fast gradient method needs O(eps^(-2/(3p-2))) iterations, and it is open whether problem structure can beat this.
XvblPIlleK.method: The authors characterize a family of smooth approximations based on p-Huber smoothing that attains the exact optimal one-sided approximation-smoothness trade-off, and combine it with accelerated proximal gradients. A matching lower bound shows the resulting rate is optimal.
XvblPIlleK.key_idea: Replace the Hölder-smooth l_p loss with a p-Huber smooth approximation at the optimal approximation-smoothness trade-off, then apply accelerated proximal gradient.
XvblPIlleK.evidence: Theory (upper bound and matching lower bound) plus numerical experiments on synthetic and real data.
XvblPIlleK.claimed_gains: Attains an epsilon-optimal solution in O(eps^(-1/p)) matrix-vector products, versus O(eps^(-2/(3p-2))) iterations for the universal method.

8INk8tEqYf.one_liner: Reward model for panoramic image generation scoring 3D consistency, polar visual quality, and image-text consistency with preference-conditioned weights.
8INk8tEqYf.problem: Panoramic image generation lacks a reliable reward model, which caps achievable performance.
8INk8tEqYf.method: PanoReward evaluates panoramic output along three axes (3D consistency, polar visual quality, image-text consistency) with adaptive, preference-conditioned weighting across task requirements. It is trained on PanoReward-Data, with 943,074 task-profile training instances derived from 195,930 source pairs.
8INk8tEqYf.key_idea: Score panoramas along three complementary axes and weight them adaptively by task profile, so one reward model reflects different judgment standards.
8INk8tEqYf.evidence: Trained on 943,074 task-profile instances from 195,930 source pairs; shows alignment with human preferences under different task requirements and supports reward-driven post-training (no specific benchmarks named).
8INk8tEqYf.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports only 'strong and consistent alignment with human preferences').

ljfvoXZSkF.one_liner: Models Granger influence between event types as a neural field over time and system state, with separate background drift.
ljfvoXZSkF.problem: Segmentation- and regime-based approaches to non-stationary event logs absorb within-segment background drift into influence estimates, producing spurious edges.
ljfvoXZSkF.method: CausalField is a point-process framework that parameterizes a continuous influence field C(t,z) with a coordinate-based neural network learned directly from the point-process likelihood, modeling background drift separately. Under stated conditions the population field identifies a direct state-conditional Granger graph on the visited region.
ljfvoXZSkF.key_idea: Represent causal influence as a continuous coordinate-network field over time and system state, fit by point-process likelihood alongside a separate time-varying background.
ljfvoXZSkF.evidence: Synthetic data, where it recovers the influence field and reproduces the predicted failure of discretized alternatives, and a real alarm log, where state conditioning improves held-out fit over static and time-only variants.
ljfvoXZSkF.claimed_gains: Remains competitive for thresholded static-graph recovery on a real alarm log and improves held-out fit with state conditioning over static and time-only variants (no numbers stated).

8c7N82wNIr.one_liner: DVGT-World jointly supervises current-geometry reconstruction and future-geometry prediction with learnable future queries, then fine-tunes for driving planning.
8c7N82wNIr.problem: Vision-Geometry-Action driving models reconstruct only currently observed scenes and lack explicit future 3D dynamics, while world-action models forecast in 2D image or latent space without explicit 3D geometric supervision.
8c7N82wNIr.method: Learnable future queries conditioned on the target horizon are added to the geometry transformer to predict future dense pointmaps and ego poses from historical multi-view observations; after geometry pretraining the model is fine-tuned for planning with future prediction disabled at inference.
8c7N82wNIr.key_idea: Add horizon-conditioned future queries to a geometry transformer so future pointmaps and ego poses are supervised alongside current geometry, then drop prediction at planning inference.
8c7N82wNIr.evidence: Multi-view future geometry prediction and closed-loop planning on NAVSIM v1 and v2.
8c7N82wNIr.claimed_gains: 93.3 PDMS on NAVSIM v1 and 90.7 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2.

5FeBsrvjii.one_liner: Extends a pretrained VLM into a unified understanding-generation model sharing ViT and backbone, with a pixel diffusion head.
5FeBsrvjii.problem: Unified multimodal models often separate visual representations or backbone computation for understanding and generation, while pixel-space generation is hard to optimize and VLM compression can discard spatial detail needed for synthesis.
5FeBsrvjii.method: HiUni reuses the same language-aligned ViT and dense Transformer backbone for both capabilities and confines task-specific computation to the output side. A Pixel Diffusion Head handles direct pixel-space optimization, and a lightweight HiGate pathway supplies fine-grained spatial details near the output stage.
5FeBsrvjii.key_idea: Share the ViT and dense backbone fully across understanding and generation, adding only a pixel diffusion head and a HiGate detail pathway at the output.
5FeBsrvjii.evidence: Experiments on understanding, image generation and editing, plus controlled comparisons of a single dense backbone supporting both capabilities (abstract truncated).
5FeBsrvjii.claimed_gains: A similar average understanding score to the pretrained VLM and competitive image generation and editing performance, with no numbers stated.

jzFZRdpuLV.one_liner: Closed-form forecaster with at most 31 parameters that models only the phase-recurrent Structure component of a series.
jzFZRdpuLV.problem: Aggregate metrics reveal little about what information lightweight and complex long-term forecasting models recover or why their performance differs.
jzFZRdpuLV.method: Decomposes the true future and model predictions into Structure and Dynamics using phase recurrence across cycles, and decomposes MSE by orthogonality. TinyCycle then models Structure directly, fit in closed form, without complex temporal mappings.
jzFZRdpuLV.key_idea: Model only the phase-recurrent Structure component of the series, because diagnostics show models recover Structure far better than Dynamics.
jzFZRdpuLV.evidence: Diagnostics across multiple models using the Structure-Dynamics MSE decomposition, and experiments comparing TinyCycle with mainstream forecasting models.
jzFZRdpuLV.claimed_gains: Recovers most of the forecasting performance of mainstream time-series models with no more than 31 parameters using closed-form fitting.

3YkirBMDWU.one_liner: Retrieves query-relevant local priors via adaptive-granularity cross-view correspondences to guide residual diffusion that fills missing view representations.
3YkirBMDWU.problem: Recovering missing representations from shared semantics alone does not capture the target view's local structure, and view heterogeneity makes reliable local correspondences across views hard to establish.
3YkirBMDWU.method: GRADE builds local regions per view at adaptive granularities and uses jointly observed members as evidence for soft cross-view correspondences, which retrieve local priors from the target view. It maps shared semantics of observed views to a target-view base representation and uses a residual diffusion guided by the priors to generate only the target-specific local information the base misses.
3YkirBMDWU.key_idea: Generate only the residual between a shared-semantics base representation and the target view, using diffusion conditioned on retrieved adaptive-granularity local priors.
3YkirBMDWU.evidence: Experiments on eight multi-view benchmark datasets across multiple missing rates.

I0smGYI9bJ.one_liner: Uses shared anchors to transfer fine-to-coarse relation structures to samples, then fuses them by adaptive low-rank consensus learning.
I0smGYI9bJ.problem: View incompleteness causes cross-view reference inconsistency, because relations depend on different observed subsets, and cross-granularity instability, because fine structures are sensitive to missingness and coarse ones can drift semantically.
I0smGYI9bJ.method: AMGC builds masked sample-anchor assignments over shared anchors and aggregates them into a sample-complete global reference without imputing missing views, then extracts fine-to-coarse structures on compact anchor graphs and transfers them to samples while preserving sparse local geometry. Adaptive low-rank consensus learning weights each view-granularity pair by its consistency with the evolving consensus.
I0smGYI9bJ.key_idea: Use shared anchors as one relational reference so multi-granularity structures extracted on anchor graphs transfer to samples without imputing missing views.
I0smGYI9bJ.evidence: Not stated; the abstract is truncated before any datasets, baselines or results.

McyllB4POR.one_liner: Training-free LLM reasoning that uses answer-token entropy to decide between direct solving and further problem decomposition.
McyllB4POR.problem: Choosing a suitable degree of decomposition by subproblem difficulty, and limiting the effect of intermediate-answer errors on the final result, remain challenging for LLM reasoning.
McyllB4POR.method: DART probes the model once, calibrates model capability regions by clustering, and uses answer-token entropy (mean token-distribution entropy over positions in a generated answer) to choose direct solving or further decomposition. A confidence-aligned self-critique constrains candidate evaluation scores and score-token confidence to guide refinement of intermediate answers.
McyllB4POR.key_idea: Answer-token entropy, calibrated into capability regions by clustering after one-time probing, gates direct solving versus decomposition, with self-critique aligned to score-token confidence.
McyllB4POR.evidence: Results aggregated across three structured tasks with multiple backbones, plus DeepMath (abstract truncated).
McyllB4POR.claimed_gains: Reduces average error by 22%-33% and average online inference cost by 23%-72% relative to the lowest-error baseline on each backbone across three structured tasks, and reports the highest accuracy on DeepMath (truncated).

Pv7EP7ebxg.one_liner: Read-through lens passes intermediate ViT patch states through the terminal layers that write into CLS before applying the classifier.
Pv7EP7ebxg.problem: Projecting intermediate ViT representations directly through the final classifier, as a logit lens, is routinely used but can mislead because the classifier reads only the CLS stream while image information sits in patch tokens.
Pv7EP7ebxg.method: A causal analysis on five ViT backbones finds that class evidence develops in the patch stream and is written into CLS only through a few terminal layers, the read window. RTLens passes intermediate patch states through this read window before the classifier, and an anatomy-based attention map exactly decomposes patch contributions to the prediction through it.
Pv7EP7ebxg.key_idea: Route intermediate patch states through the terminal read window that writes into CLS before classifying, instead of projecting them directly.
Pv7EP7ebxg.evidence: Causal analyses and comparisons across five ViT backbones.
Pv7EP7ebxg.claimed_gains: Across all five backbones, RTLens predictions match the model's causal behavior far better than direct projection and the attention map localizes the evidence the model uses more accurately, with no numbers stated.

0Ig477ud8W.one_liner: Sparse MoE with differentiable ReLU routing, learnable expert-wise scaling and NormSiLU non-gated experts to match dense models.
0Ig477ud8W.problem: Existing sparse MoE designs leave a quality gap to dense Transformers at equal total parameters, because hard TopK blocks gradients and fixes one activation ratio per token, or heavy sparsity regularization costs performance.
0Ig477ud8W.method: DECO lets sparsity arise from differentiable ReLU-based routing, with learnable expert-wise scaling that balances routed against shared experts. Its experts are non-gated MLPs whose NormSiLU activation keeps the routed-expert activation ratio low and stable, so only light regularization is needed.
0Ig477ud8W.key_idea: Replace hard TopK routing with differentiable ReLU routing and use NormSiLU in non-gated experts to keep activation sparsity low and stable under light regularization.
0Ig477ud8W.evidence: Experiments under a matched total parameter budget and identical training tokens, showing that established MoE baselines leave a gap to an equally budgeted dense model (abstract truncated).

D2YgKYmfm4.one_liner: Embodied VLM trained as four RLVR specialists merged by weight merging and routed distillation into one model.
D2YgKYmfm4.problem: Embodied capabilities are usually developed against isolated task-specific objectives, leaving open how to organize and integrate them around iterative robot execution.
D2YgKYmfm4.method: Capek 0.5 organizes training by an execution-centric taxonomy of four capability families: Spatial Reasoning, Temporal Understanding, Action Guidance and State Verification. Each capability is acquired by a dedicated specialist through reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards from a shared backbone, then the specialists are consolidated by weight-space merging followed by routed policy-space distillation.
D2YgKYmfm4.key_idea: Train per-capability RLVR specialists from a shared backbone and consolidate them with weight-space merging followed by routed policy-space distillation.
D2YgKYmfm4.evidence: Evaluated from three perspectives, including comprehensive benchmark suites and Capek-StateBench, a new benchmark (abstract truncated).

tU0NdZmxRD.one_liner: Tokenizes the globe into latitude rings and stacks weight-shared palindromic zonal and meridional operators for global S2S forecasting.
tU0NdZmxRD.problem: Existing geometry-aware S2S forecasting methods do not specify how the zonal and meridional interactions governing atmospheric dynamics should be explicitly coordinated and composed.
tU0NdZmxRD.method: AnisoCast uses an Anisotropic Embedding that tokenizes the global grid into latitudinal rings to preserve zonal periodic structure, and stacked Aniso Blocks that arrange latent Zonal and Meridional Operators in a weight-shared palindromic composition inspired by symmetric operator splitting.
tU0NdZmxRD.key_idea: Compose zonal and meridional operators in a weight-shared palindromic order, as in symmetric operator splitting, over latitude-ring tokens.
tU0NdZmxRD.evidence: Experiments on the ERA5 reanalysis dataset comparing forecasting accuracy and computational efficiency against existing methods.

Umr7o4QlqL.one_liner: Interleaves frozen-LLM Transformer layers with repeated reads of a persistent graph memory using query states refined by earlier layers.
Umr7o4QlqL.problem: Existing approaches expose graph information to LLMs as retrieved text or a fixed representation formed before reasoning, so graph evidence cannot adapt to the evolving language-model state.
Umr7o4QlqL.method: ReGraph keeps a persistent graph memory outside the LLM context and repeatedly queries it with graph-query states refined by preceding Transformer layers, so each read depends on the instruction and the evidence acquired so far. A query-conditioned topology diffusion mechanism couples semantic relevance with graph structure while the pretrained LLM stays frozen.
Umr7o4QlqL.key_idea: Interleave graph reads with intermediate LLM computation, using layer-refined query states and query-conditioned topology diffusion over a persistent graph memory.
Umr7o4QlqL.evidence: Experiments on six benchmarks, including two introduced in this work, across open-ended graph reasoning settings.

l5NfZoPKFW.one_liner: Query-side low-rank adapters learn to read frozen position-independent KV caches, distilled from full-prefill outputs, with no cache recomputation.
l5NfZoPKFW.problem: Position-independent caching of reusable artifacts loses quality versus full-context prefill, and existing fixes restore global position IDs or recompute selected tokens.
l5NfZoPKFW.method: Attuner inserts low-rank adapters into the query projections and trains them by distilling the full-prefill distribution into the student. At inference it needs no cache recomputation.
l5NfZoPKFW.key_idea: The quality loss comes from attention scores, not cached KV, so adapt query projections with LoRA distilled from full-prefill to read frozen caches.
l5NfZoPKFW.evidence: Diagnostic analysis showing positional mismatch has minor effect and that replacing PIC attention scores with full-prefill scores recovers performance; the evaluation details are cut off.
l5NfZoPKFW.claimed_gains: Trains fewer than 0.05% of model parameters and recovers near-full-prefill quality at position-independent-caching efficiency; quality numbers are not stated.

GMRGQIf7n4.one_liner: Predicts the kernel representation of JEPA latent targets so the predictor recovers a conditional kernel mean embedding.
GMRGQIf7n4.problem: Standard JEPA objectives are point estimation, so the optimal predictor gives one summary of the conditional target distribution, which cannot identify that distribution when several targets are plausible.
GMRGQIf7n4.method: K-JEPA applies a characteristic-kernel transformation to JEPA latent targets and predicts the kernel representation of the target instead of the target itself, leaving the architecture and prediction setup unchanged.
GMRGQIf7n4.key_idea: Predict the kernel feature map of the latent target under a characteristic kernel, so the population target becomes the conditional kernel mean embedding that uniquely identifies the distribution.
GMRGQIf7n4.evidence: A proof about the population target, controlled settings, a target-retrieval comparison across JEPA formulations and modalities, and probabilistic scoring, calibration, and selective evaluations.

LhzycTQBqu.one_liner: Closed-loop evaluation framework for full-duplex omni models using an event-driven user simulator, environment emulator, and timeline DSL.
LhzycTQBqu.problem: Replaying predefined input trajectories cannot test full-duplex omni models in evolving interactions where users interrupt, revise requests, and resume earlier tasks.
LhzycTQBqu.method: OmniGym represents each test case as an executable episode, with an event-driven user simulator and a tunable environment emulator on a shared timeline; a timeline DSL captures model-dependent triggers and scoring criteria so interaction logic runs reproducibly across models.
LhzycTQBqu.key_idea: Make test cases executable episodes in which a simulated user and environment react to the model's responses through timeline-DSL triggers.
LhzycTQBqu.evidence: 600 test cases built from 200 base scenarios across three matched severity levels and seven distractor categories, evaluating four systems from the Qwen, Gemini, and GLM families.

EmVTVcyZwW.one_liner: Efficient randomized forecaster achieving O(T^{2/3-eps}) expected calibration error by adding a Blackwell-style correction layer to SPR-Calibration.
EmVTVcyZwW.problem: A recent result broke the classical T^{2/3} barrier for online binary calibration error, and this paper asks for a computationally efficient forecaster that attains error below that barrier.
EmVTVcyZwW.method: Combines the SPR-Calibration procedure, which controls calibration against a surrogate sequence of conditional-mean estimates, with an outer Blackwell-style correction layer that controls the extra error from approximating true outcomes by the surrogates. The analysis splits total error into surrogate calibration error and the residual discrepancy between surrogates and outcomes.
EmVTVcyZwW.key_idea: Layer a Blackwell-style correction over SPR-Calibration to control the gap between the surrogate sequence and true outcomes, using a quadratic potential argument and the sparsity of the SPR forecaster.
EmVTVcyZwW.evidence: Theoretical analysis only; no experiments are stated.
EmVTVcyZwW.claimed_gains: An efficient randomized forecaster with computationally expected calibration error O(T^{2/3-eps}) for some constant eps > 0.

qN4PNTc1kh.one_liner: QDGL fuses missing or noisy modalities via Hilbert-sphere encoding and a dual vector and density-state graph path.
qN4PNTc1kh.problem: Missing modality features limit biomedical triadic prediction, and fusing modalities into one vector lets graph propagation spread one modality's error to neighbors.
qN4PNTc1kh.method: Hilbert-sphere encoding maps modalities to a shared complex unit sphere; adaptive fusion builds vector representations and mixed density states, and a density path propagates states with relation-specific unitary transformations and Hilbert-Schmidt overlap.
qN4PNTc1kh.key_idea: Keep each modality as a separate weighted component of a density state propagated by unitary transformations, so a noisy modality only alters its own overlap terms.
qN4PNTc1kh.evidence: not stated in the visible abstract, which is cut off before the experiments.

Img6B2vgpk.one_liner: Predicts action-induced future information in latent space with a large multimodal model instead of generating future GUI screens.
Img6B2vgpk.problem: Pixel-space GUI world models pay high reconstruction cost, must reproduce appearance detail not needed for action selection, and suffer an identity shortcut where predictions copy the current state.
Img6B2vgpk.method: A large multimodal model serves as the latent world model with two heads: a latent action head for action selection and a transition head for action-conditioned future information. An action-aware contrastive objective pushes transition representations to capture discriminative action-induced changes.
Img6B2vgpk.key_idea: Shift the prediction target from full-screen reconstruction to action-conditioned latent transitions, trained with an action-aware contrastive loss to avoid the identity shortcut.
Img6B2vgpk.evidence: The abstract mentions extensive experiments across offline settings but is cut off before any datasets or results.

6x3Gd6UO3e.one_liner: Applies an unrestricted dense convolution kernel directly to CP-factorized inputs, equivalent to dense convolution without reconstructing the tensor.
6x3Gd6UO3e.problem: Convolutional learning on high-dimensional data is limited by the cost of materializing dense inputs and intermediate tensors.
6x3Gd6UO3e.method: CP-Conv applies a trainable convolutional kernel directly to Canonical Polyadic factors, algebraically equivalent to dense convolution on the represented tensor. CCP-Conv fuses the convolution with learnable mode-wise compression to produce compact outputs without materializing the full convolution result.
6x3Gd6UO3e.key_idea: Compute convolution on CP factors mode by mode so the dense tensor is never formed, and fuse mode-wise compression into the same operator.
6x3Gd6UO3e.evidence: Synthetic data, UCF101, Ego4D, seven-dimensional Fokker-Planck problems, and operator identification on perturbed PDEBench-derived shallow-water fields, benchmarked against dense, FFT-based, and cuDNN convolution.
6x3Gd6UO3e.claimed_gains: CCP-Conv processes implicit tensors containing up to 2.94x10^11 values, and in a stride-matched R3D-18 experiment on UCF101 it achieves comparable classification accuracy with 25.2% less cumulative training time.

a3QffHWDuN.one_liner: Self-play Approximate Value Iteration with one-step greedy lookahead rivals AlphaZero-style MCTS at substantially lower training and inference cost.
a3QffHWDuN.problem: MCTS-based self-play methods carry substantial computational overhead, and it is unclear whether simpler methods stay competitive in moderately sized games.
a3QffHWDuN.method: A minimal self-play implementation of Approximate Value Iteration is trained on Connect Four, Hex (7x7) and synthetic games, with ground-truth oracles for exact evaluation; policies act greedily with one-step lookahead.
a3QffHWDuN.key_idea: Learn state values by self-play approximate value iteration and act greedily with one-step lookahead, with no tree search, evaluated against exact oracles.
a3QffHWDuN.evidence: Connect Four, Hex (7x7) and synthetic games with ground-truth oracles, plus preliminary experiments on Othello and Go (9x9).
a3QffHWDuN.claimed_gains: AVI learns more accurate value functions than AlphaZero and its greedy policies stay competitive with MCTS-based policies at substantially lower training and inference costs; no numbers stated.

eerUF6J6va.one_liner: Defines an orbit stabilisation entropy and shows parameter-tied equivariant circuits, not state-level symmetry, transfer symmetry to learned functions.
eerUF6J6va.problem: It is unclear whether state-level symmetry is sufficient to produce symmetry of the learned function in quantum learning.
eerUF6J6va.method: Defines an orbit stabilisation entropy and an average stabilisation weight (equal to the purity of the group-twirled state) and proves an entropic orbit-stabiliser identity. It tests soft regularisation with these quantities, then derives sufficient conditions for exact function-level symmetry and implements them by parameter tying across five finite groups.
eerUF6J6va.key_idea: An entropy identity extends the orbit-stabiliser theorem to quantum states, and exact function-level equivariance via parameter tying, not state-level symmetry, guarantees symmetry transfer.
eerUF6J6va.evidence: Controlled quantum learning experiments over Z2, Z4, V4, Z6 and S3 comparing soft regularisation with hard-equivariant parameter tying.
eerUF6J6va.claimed_gains: Proves H_stab = log|Stab_G([psi])| + H(q) for any finite group; soft regularisation gave no statistically robust generalisation gain, and the size of the hard-equivariant gain is cut off in the abstract.

pLN4G11OVu.one_liner: Characterizes GNN classifiers preserved under embeddings, injective homomorphisms or homomorphisms as fragments of graded modal logic, independent of architecture.
pLN4G11OVu.problem: Known GNN-logic correspondences depend on fixed architectural choices such as aggregation, combination and activation functions, so they cover only restricted GNN classes.
pLN4G11OVu.method: The paper takes a semantic view: for GNN classifiers preserved under embeddings, injective homomorphisms and homomorphisms, it shows each class corresponds to existential graded modal logic, its existential-positive fragment, and existential-positive modal logic. It also shows each class admits a GNN architecture of the same expressiveness.
pLN4G11OVu.key_idea: Characterize GNN classes by their preservation under structural maps and use a new well-quasi-order on bounded-height trees to get finite representations of the corresponding logic fragments.
pLN4G11OVu.evidence: Theoretical proofs of logical characterizations; no experiments are described.

7OVx7WQ0Lf.one_liner: Block-autoregressive flow language model converted from a pretrained 8B autoregressive model, unifying next-token, flow, confidence, and self-speculative decoding.
7OVx7WQ0Lf.problem: Flow language models denoise all positions synchronously, which conflicts with left-to-right text, and have stayed at sub-billion scale without competitive quality-speed tradeoffs.
7OVx7WQ0Lf.method: Lafa preserves causal order across blocks while learning an asynchronous progression within each block, and keeps both a block denoiser and a next-token predictor. It is scaled to 8B parameters by converting a pretrained autoregressive model using less than 10B training tokens.
7OVx7WQ0Lf.key_idea: Blockwise causal ordering with asynchronous within-block flow progression, plus a retained next-token predictor, lets one model switch among sequential, parallel, confidence, and self-speculative decoding.
7OVx7WQ0Lf.evidence: Six benchmarks spanning instruction following, reasoning, and code, where the different decoding modes trace a quality-speed Pareto frontier.
7OVx7WQ0Lf.claimed_gains: Attains 2.54x the throughput of a strong autoregressive baseline at matched quality.

ED8cESDEp6.one_liner: Uses verified emotion outcomes online to reallocate which interaction conditions an empathetic dialogue policy practices next, alongside RL training.
ED8cESDEp6.problem: RL with verifiable feedback updates parameters but leaves the distribution of later experience fixed, which limits multi-turn empathetic dialogue where the training value of interaction conditions changes as the policy improves.
ED8cESDEp6.method: Continuous outcomes train the dialogue policy, while thresholded group outcomes estimate the training value of reusable intent-state units and reallocate future interactions. Hierarchical evidence sharing stabilizes sparse estimates, and uncertainty-guided exploration with uniform rehearsal preserves coverage, with simulator and verifier frozen.
ED8cESDEp6.key_idea: Thresholded group emotion outcomes estimate the training value of intent-state units, and future rollouts are reallocated by that estimated value under a fixed rollout budget.
ED8cESDEp6.evidence: Evaluated on SAGE with Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-4B against protocol-matched uniform emotion-reward RL, plus cross-benchmark and human evaluations.
ED8cESDEp6.claimed_gains: On SAGE, raises Qwen3-8B Overall from 53.87 to 79.24, outperforming protocol-matched uniform emotion-reward RL by 7.23 points, and by 4.14 points at Qwen3-4B.

3bFHWXSkAf.one_liner: Representer point selection by tracking a regularized gradient trajectory anchored to the target model's weights, avoiding Hessian-vector products.
3bFHWXSkAf.problem: Existing sample-attribution methods need performance-altering regularization, rely on costly Hessian-vector products, or fail to reconstruct the original parameters, so they explain a surrogate rather than the actual model.
3bFHWXSkAf.method: RPS-TrReg identifies sample importance by tracing a regularized optimization path toward the original model's parameter state, with a regularization term that keeps tracking anchored to the target model's weights. This yields a decomposition of the target model into a linear combination of training samples without second-order derivatives.
3bFHWXSkAf.key_idea: A regularized optimization path tracked toward the target model's parameters decomposes the model into a linear combination of training samples, with the regularizer anchoring it to the original weights.
3bFHWXSkAf.evidence: The visible abstract is cut off at the empirical results; datasets, models, and baselines are not stated.

U1EpjzED1C.one_liner: Any-to-any multimodal generation as conditional flow inference over one canonical latent, trained by self-distillation from richer-evidence predictions.
U1EpjzED1C.problem: Flexible any-to-any generation must condition on arbitrary subsets of modalities and keep generated targets consistent, while training examples are incomplete.
U1EpjzED1C.method: MUNITE models the conditional distribution over the latent of the complete observation given any modality subset in a single conditional flow model, with a shared latent sample for cross-target consistency and modality-specific decoders for the remaining uncertainty. It extends conditional flow matching through self-distillation, where predictions conditioned on richer observations supervise the same model on smaller subsets at the same latent state.
U1EpjzED1C.key_idea: Treat encoding and generation as one inference problem with varying observed evidence, and train subset-conditioned flows to match flows conditioned on richer evidence at the same latent state.
U1EpjzED1C.evidence: PolyMNIST-D-Q, FFHQ64, and image-text-audio experiments (abstract truncated).
U1EpjzED1C.claimed_gains: Competitive or better generation quality and source-target alignment with higher joint-generation coherence; no numbers are visible in the abstract.

onh0OoRi1h.one_liner: Refines post-training ternary LLMs by relocating side-state assignments ranked with one gradient taken at the quantized model.
onh0OoRi1h.problem: Post-training ternarization produces a compact discrete model whose ternary assignment need not be optimal for the target task.
onh0OoRi1h.method: TernRefine computes a single task gradient G at the deployed quantized model, ranks legal relocations by the first-order score −⟨G, ∆Q⟩, and applies a number of relocations chosen on a separate validation split. It preserves the ternary codebook and the exact number of side states in every quantization group.
onh0OoRi1h.key_idea: Rank legal side-state relocations by the first-order score −⟨G, ∆Q⟩, with G evaluated at the quantized model rather than at the full-precision model.
onh0OoRi1h.evidence: A controlled study over five fitting offsets compares quantized-model and full-precision gradients, and WikiText-2 and C4 are evaluated on OPT-350M, Llama-2-7B, and Qwen3-8B after affine ternarization, on PT2-initialized models, and on zero-shot tasks.
onh0OoRi1h.claimed_gains: Patches from quantized-model and full-precision gradients have less than 2% Jaccard overlap, and ranking with the quantized-model gradient improves WikiText-2 in all five runs while the full-precision gradient degrades it on average.

zEK0AxR5OL.one_liner: Graph foundation model pre-training with two coordinators for high- and low-concordance nodes, soft-routed per node by structural concordance.
zEK0AxR5OL.problem: Cross-domain graph foundation models organize transfer at the graph level and overlook node-level structural heterogeneity.
zEK0AxR5OL.method: The paper defines structural concordance, the local agreement between a node's topological and feature-induced neighborhoods, and pre-trains with two coordinators specialized for high- and low-concordance regimes combined by node-wise soft routing. Graph-specific meta coordinators integrate concordance-conditioned information and mediate communication across source domains while preserving original topologies.
zEK0AxR5OL.key_idea: Route each node softly between high- and low-concordance coordinators by its structural concordance, with meta coordinators linking domains without homogenizing graph topologies.
zEK0AxR5OL.evidence: Theory on informativeness, estimability, and representation stability of concordance-aware coordination, plus experiments across diverse graph benchmarks (details cut off in the provided abstract).

VYIarfuZvr.one_liner: Weights RL credit by traced token dependencies and blocks joint commitment of dependent tokens in masked image generation.
VYIarfuZvr.problem: Coarse credit assignment ignores the unequal downstream importance of committed tokens, and confidence-based decoding may jointly commit strongly dependent tokens.
VYIarfuZvr.method: During RL post-training, Dep2C-Credit traces dependencies from future prompt-relevant predictions back to committed tokens and accumulates them along the trajectory to guide hierarchical credit allocation. At inference, Dep2C-Decoding ranks candidates by confidence and dependency degree and uses pairwise dependencies to constrain joint commitment.
VYIarfuZvr.key_idea: Trace dependencies backward from future prompt-relevant predictions to committed tokens to weight credit, and use pairwise dependencies to block joint commitment of coupled tokens.
VYIarfuZvr.evidence: Experiments on Show-o and Lumina-DiMOO measuring compositional generation and complex prompt following with GenEval and DPG-Bench.
VYIarfuZvr.claimed_gains: GenEval scores of 0.86 and 0.92 and DPG-Bench scores of 84.37 and 83.69 on Show-o and Lumina-DiMOO, respectively.

HFDcgwr5dU.one_liner: Corrects learned joint rotations with reliability-gated alignment to predicted global bone directions for monocular mocap on arbitrary skeletons.
HFDcgwr5dU.problem: Joint-rotation errors are coupled across the skeleton and propagate along the kinematic hierarchy, hurting motion recovery when the target topology differs from the video subject.
HFDcgwr5dU.method: CAST combines learned local rotations with a geometric correction module (GRACE) that, guided by an observability analysis, aligns composed orientations in parent-to-child order using predicted global bone directions and leaves unconstrained components to the learned predictor. The predictor and correction are trained jointly with motion-derived supervision on a frozen image encoder.
HFDcgwr5dU.key_idea: Gate the correction of composed joint orientations by reliability of predicted global bone directions, applied parent-to-child to limit error propagation.
HFDcgwr5dU.evidence: TopoCap evaluation protocol including unseen topologies, a curated Mixamo cross-skeleton benchmark, and a user preference study.
HFDcgwr5dU.claimed_gains: The causal CAST-B variant achieves over 51 FPS on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU; accuracy gains are not quantified in the visible abstract.

Fw2Qfz1OrM.one_liner: Solves translation averaging by assigning each camera a sphere-grid cell from K reference points and intersecting the resulting rays robustly.
Fw2Qfz1OrM.problem: Convex relaxations tolerate only about a third of wrong pairwise directions and robust local optimisers only refine their initial guess, while discrete search needs a bounded candidate set that camera positions lack.
Fw2Qfz1OrM.method: Plant K reference points and, for each, globally assign every camera the cell of a fixed unit-sphere grid in which it is seen. Each assignment pins a camera to a ray, and robustly intersecting its K rays gives its 3D position.
Fw2Qfz1OrM.key_idea: Replace unbounded 3D position search with discrete inference over a bounded sphere grid of viewing directions from K reference points, then intersect rays.
Fw2Qfz1OrM.evidence: not stated (the abstract is cut off before the experiments).

8aRfNsLiHh.one_liner: Trains a wavefield neural operator on Convergent Born Series fixed-point residuals instead of paired labels, then uses it for inversion.
8aRfNsLiHh.problem: Deep-learning full waveform inversion faces scarce labels, unstable physics-constrained training, and difficulty enforcing open boundaries under broadband settings.
8aRfNsLiHh.method: CBNO minimizes a Convergent Born Series fixed-point discrepancy with Perfectly Matched Layers as the physical training signal, using frequency-partitioned Axial-AFNO experts with shared low-rank projections and axis- and wavenumber-aware gates. The frozen surrogate is used in differentiable inversion with upgoing-wave separation to emphasize weak reflections.
8aRfNsLiHh.key_idea: Use CBS fixed-point consistency as a label-free physics loss for a frequency-partitioned neural operator, then freeze it as a differentiable forward model for inversion.
8aRfNsLiHh.evidence: Forward modeling on OpenFWI, and zero-shot transfer of the frozen surrogate to inversion on 2D Marmousi and Overthrust benchmarks.
8aRfNsLiHh.claimed_gains: About 10x forward-modeling speedup over the CBS reference solver and about 12x inversion speedup over CBS-based AD-FWI at a fixed budget of 50 velocity updates.

W0sjNP3Ko9.one_liner: Reconstructs time-varying hair geometry from multi-view videos using a Strand Gaussian representation.
W0sjNP3Ko9.problem: Existing dynamic hair methods add learned dynamics to static reconstruction and struggle to balance frame-wise photometric fidelity with optimization efficiency.
W0sjNP3Ko9.method: A Strand Gaussian based framework reconstructs time-varying hair geometry while keeping photometric fidelity on the observed sequence and preserving photorealistic appearance. The abstract gives no further detail on the dynamics model or optimization.
W0sjNP3Ko9.key_idea: Strand Gaussians serve as the hair representation for time-varying reconstruction from multi-view video; the abstract does not describe the mechanism further.
W0sjNP3Ko9.evidence: Qualitative and quantitative evaluation on the public NeRSemble dataset.
W0sjNP3Ko9.claimed_gains: Claims reconstruction quality that outperforms prior methods by a significant margin; no numbers stated.

xHVHpXULAJ.one_liner: Dynamically evolves the semantic view space with View Expansion and View Contraction, then completes missing views for clustering.
xHVHpXULAJ.problem: Incomplete multi-view clustering faces missing views and cross-view semantic redundancy, and existing methods fuse information within a fixed view space, making it hard to explore complementary semantics.
xHVHpXULAJ.method: SVE_IMVC learns initial semantic representations through cross-view mutual information learning, then applies View Expansion to explore complementary semantics and View Contraction to suppress redundant representations. Missing views are recovered through semantic-guided completion from the evolved global semantic representation, and the completed representations are clustered.
xHVHpXULAJ.key_idea: Let the semantic view space change during training, expanding it to add complementary semantics and contracting it to remove redundancy, instead of fusing within a fixed view space.
xHVHpXULAJ.evidence: Experimental results on incomplete multi-view data; datasets and baselines are not stated.
xHVHpXULAJ.claimed_gains: Claims effectively improved clustering performance on incomplete multi-view data; no numbers stated.

PVp2s3KOp9.one_liner: Benchmark of 2,740 image-editing instances with shared atomic-requirement checklists, plus a multi-agent framework that turns failures into training data.
PVp2s3KOp9.problem: Aggregate scores in image-editing evaluation obscure unmet requirements, and evaluation needs to reveal local failures and translate them into priorities for model improvement.
PVp2s3KOp9.method: WeGenEditBench covers 148 task types across single-image, text-intensive, and multi-reference editing, with pre-generated checklists decomposing each request into atomic requirements linked to visual evidence. WeGenEvoStudio combines failure analysis, retrieval-grounded data construction, supervised adaptation, and re-evaluation in a multi-agent framework.
PVp2s3KOp9.key_idea: Checklists of atomic requirements localize editing failures, and a multi-agent loop of failure analysis, retrieval-grounded data construction, and supervised adaptation converts them into training priorities.
PVp2s3KOp9.evidence: 15 evaluated configurations on the benchmark, plus adaptation tested across four generation and editing benchmarks.
PVp2s3KOp9.claimed_gains: GPT-Image-2 leads single-image editing with an Overall score of 4.076 and Seedream-5.0-Pro leads text-intensive editing at 4.291, while on the report-selected Top-5 targets FLUX.2 [dev] improves Overall from 1.083 to 3.517 and Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 gains 13.2%.

5IQp6EOHry.one_liner: Speculative-decoding drafter that separates recurrent trajectory state from token prediction and expands high-confidence draft branches progressively.
5IQp6EOHry.problem: Autoregressive drafters such as EAGLE-3 share one hidden state for token prediction and recurrent propagation, and high token accuracy can coexist with substantial recurrent-state deviation from target-model features.
5IQp6EOHry.method: STEP is a feature-logit disentangled drafter that uses separate representations for trajectory evolution and token prediction, with a staged feature-alignment curriculum that uses target-model fused features as an early reference before removing the constraint. It adds confidence-guided progressive tree expansion that extends promising branches for longer accepted continuations.
5IQp6EOHry.key_idea: Separate the feature stream that evolves the draft trajectory from the logit stream that predicts tokens, aligning features to the target model early in training and then releasing the constraint.
5IQp6EOHry.evidence: Four target models, five benchmarks, and two temperatures (40 settings), plus ablations and SGLang throughput measurements.
5IQp6EOHry.claimed_gains: Outperforms EAGLE-3 in all 40 settings with average relative gains of 10.1% in decoding speed and 15.1% in acceptance length, and 2.9-11.9% higher throughput in SGLang.

y4TCdn8fmL.one_liner: Matched Invariant Interchange tests whether swapping energy-correlated units transfers donor energy to predictions more than swapping random control units.
y4TCdn8fmL.problem: Being able to decode energy from a hidden layer does not show that the model uses that physical information to predict the next state.
y4TCdn8fmL.method: MII exchanges units correlated with energy and checks whether the predicted energy tracks a donor's energy more closely than when exchanging equally many control units, a difference called correlation selectivity. It is applied to residual and direct predictors, including the Poseidon fluid model at three sizes.
y4TCdn8fmL.key_idea: Interchange energy-correlated units versus an equal number of matched control units, and read the difference in donor-energy transfer as selectivity.
y4TCdn8fmL.evidence: Poseidon fluid models at three sizes on NS-Sines and NS-Gauss, with three seeds on NS-Sines.
y4TCdn8fmL.claimed_gains: On NS-Sines, supervising Poseidon-B on kinetic energy rather than a fixed random function of the field raises encoder selectivity by 0.066-0.134 across three seeds.

0zxbqwjjB9.one_liner: Couples a belief-desire-intention Mental World Model with a policy model, trained by alternating RL phases with step-level rewards.
0zxbqwjjB9.problem: Language agents often do not maintain an explicit, evolving model of users and counterparts in their decision process, limiting adaptation as interactions evolve.
0zxbqwjjB9.method: A Mental World Model tracks beliefs, desires, and intentions from interaction history, and a Policy Model conditions on these states plus task context to act. Trajectory-level outcome feedback and step-level rewards from fixed scorers become step-wise relative advantages for RL, and the two models are trained in alternating phases.
0zxbqwjjB9.key_idea: Make the counterpart's beliefs, desires, and intentions an explicit model that the policy conditions on, and co-train the two in alternating phases with step-wise relative advantages.
0zxbqwjjB9.evidence: SOTOPIA, SOTOPIA-Hard, ALFWorld, and WebShop, with Qwen3-8B under self-play.
0zxbqwjjB9.claimed_gains: With Qwen3-8B under self-play, GOAL/OVERALL scores of 9.27/4.03 on SOTOPIA and 8.16/3.94 on SOTOPIA-Hard, and reported results on ALFWorld and WebShop exceed the evaluated general RL baselines.

TA78JcVQac.one_liner: Fully integer-only post-training quantization for diffusion transformers using runtime scale adjustment, log2 online softmax, and finer dyadic requantization.
TA78JcVQac.problem: Existing diffusion quantization still relies on floating-point operations, and integer-only frameworks do not fit modern diffusion transformers because of fixed quantization scales, no tiled-attention support, and sensitivity to activation outliers.
TA78JcVQac.method: I-DiT adds a dynamic scale adjustment that adapts to activation ranges at runtime, a log2-based online softmax for numerically stable tiled attention in integer, and a reformulated dyadic requantization enabling finer-grained activation quantization that localizes outlier impact. It needs no costly fine-tuning.
TA78JcVQac.key_idea: Adapt integer quantization scales at runtime, compute tiled softmax in integer via a log2 formulation, and requantize at finer granularity to contain outliers.
TA78JcVQac.evidence: Experiments on PixArt, SD3, and FLUX.
TA78JcVQac.claimed_gains: Claims preserved generation quality with fully integer-only inference across the tested diffusion transformers; no numbers stated.

iEin4tZoqG.one_liner: Reuses shared Transformer layers recursively during training with per-loop supervision so CTR inference can run with zero loops.
iEin4tZoqG.problem: Scaling Transformer CTR models by stacking parameters adds computational and storage overhead that conflicts with industrial deployment constraints.
iEin4tZoqG.method: LoopCTR increases training-time computation through recursive reuse of shared layers in a sandwich architecture with Hyper-Connected Residuals and Mixture-of-Experts, with process supervision at every loop depth encoding multi-loop benefits into the shared parameters. Inference then uses a train-multi-loop, infer-zero-loop strategy.
iEin4tZoqG.key_idea: Supervise every loop depth of a recursively reused layer stack so multi-loop gains are absorbed into the shared parameters and a single zero-loop forward pass suffices.
iEin4tZoqG.evidence: Three public benchmarks and one industrial dataset, plus an oracle analysis.
iEin4tZoqG.claimed_gains: A single zero-loop forward pass outperforms all baselines, and oracle analysis shows 0.02-0.04 AUC of untapped headroom.

PckoF2fJZv.one_liner: Federated minimax method using online mirror ascent with blockwise restarts, plus bidirectional error-feedback compression on dual-weighted gradients.
PckoF2fJZv.problem: Agnostic federated learning across m heterogeneous workers is bottlenecked by communication, from both the number of synchronization rounds and the per-round cost.
PckoF2fJZv.method: AFL-BR updates dual weights over workers with online mirror ascent with KL divergence and blockwise restarts. AFL-Com adds bidirectional compression with error feedback applied to dual-weighted gradients rather than local gradients, to control aggregated compression error under time-varying weights.
PckoF2fJZv.key_idea: Apply error feedback to dual-weighted gradients instead of local gradients, and update worker weights by KL mirror ascent with blockwise restarts to cut synchronization rounds.
PckoF2fJZv.evidence: Convergence theory for nonconvex stationarity rates under general delta-approximate compressors, with a sharper dependence for additive-and-idempotent compressors with shared randomness.
PckoF2fJZv.claimed_gains: AFL-BR attains an O((log m)^(1/4) T^(-1/8)) stationarity rate and AFL-Com attains O((delta^(-1) + (log m)^(1/4)) T^(-1/8)), improving the delta-dependence from delta^(-1) to delta^(-1/2) for additive-and-idempotent compressors with shared randomness.

BlHFBSfaYN.one_liner: Derives flip-coefficient and tangent-drift laws for gradient descent near the stability threshold in wide additive networks.
BlHFBSfaYN.problem: Near the stability threshold, GD on an interpolating squared loss can oscillate across minima, but local bifurcation theory covers only projected GD at a fixed minimum, not full GD that also moves along minima and changes curvature.
BlHFBSfaYN.method: In wide additive networks, shows the flip coefficient (scaled by m) and a tangent-drift coefficient are exact functionals of the blocks' empirical law at every regular interpolant. For one residual with balanced i.i.d. initialization, positive tangent drift, a near-critical step, and a moment condition, proves one GD trajectory tracks an explicit amplitude-sharpness system.
BlHFBSfaYN.key_idea: Pairing consecutive GD steps cancels the oscillation and leaves a gradient step on sharpness proportional to the squared amplitude, driving sharpness below the stability threshold.
BlHFBSfaYN.evidence: A proof of trajectory tracking with an explicit amplitude-sharpness system, plus experiments from random initialization that the abstract says confirm the theory.
BlHFBSfaYN.claimed_gains: Proves GD tracks the amplitude-sharpness system with O_P(m^(-1/2)) error over O(sqrt(m)) steps and converges to an interpolant with eta*lambda_max<2 under either flip sign.

nJnlcL9vCh.one_liner: Proves measure-dependent pushforwards uniformly approximate continuous measure-to-measure operators under a uniform level set condition, but fail for atomic inputs.
nJnlcL9vCh.problem: It is unclear when models that transform each input sample by a function depending on the whole input distribution, including measure-theoretic transformers, can approximate arbitrary continuous operators between spaces of probability measures.
nJnlcL9vCh.method: Shows universal approximation fails when atomic inputs are allowed, then introduces the uniform level set condition (a continuous measure-dependent scalarization whose shrinking level sets carry uniformly vanishing mass) and proves uniform approximation in p-Wasserstein distance on compact families satisfying it.
nJnlcL9vCh.key_idea: A uniform level set condition, a measure-dependent scalarization whose shrinking level sets carry uniformly vanishing mass, enables approximation, while atomic inputs block deterministic pushforwards from splitting mass.
nJnlcL9vCh.evidence: Theory only as stated: a counterexample with atomic inputs and a uniform approximation theorem in p-Wasserstein distance on compact families satisfying the condition.

Uo9FaHq0IN.one_liner: Plug-and-play module that predicts a stage-conditioned continuous level-of-detail field to select restoration scale per location from neighboring encoder levels.
Uo9FaHq0IN.problem: Most image restoration methods use predefined multi-scale hierarchies with fixed fusion or attention, so representation scale is set by the architecture rather than by degradation type, region, or reconstruction stage.
Uo9FaHq0IN.method: GraLoD reuses the native encoder hierarchy, aligns its multi-scale features into a shared LOD representation space, and predicts a stage-conditioned LOD field at each decoder stage, with each location continuously querying only two neighboring levels. Minimal-sufficient footprint calibration (MSFC) and structure-aware regularization (SAR) discourage degenerate or arbitrary scale selection.
Uo9FaHq0IN.key_idea: Treat restoration scale as a spatially varying, stage-dependent continuous variable, interpolating between two neighboring feature levels per location according to a predicted LOD field.
Uo9FaHq0IN.evidence: Integration into existing restoration backbones, including all-in-one restoration with heterogeneous degradations (experiment details cut off in the abstract).

ICuWlD1wKx.one_liner: Benchmark evaluating agents on 11 multi-stage professional projects with 150 interdependent subtasks, a persistent workspace, client feedback, and expert rubrics.
ICuWlD1wKx.problem: Existing benchmarks cover professional tasks and extended workflows but inadequately assess how projects evolve and whether final multi-file deliverables meet acceptance criteria.
ICuWlD1wKx.method: DeliverBench is reconstructed from real-world projects with domain experts, spanning seven domains. Agents work in a persistent workspace, incorporating new materials and client feedback released along a project timeline and reusing, revising, and integrating their own earlier artifacts, scored by expert-reviewed rubrics on checkpoints and final packages.
ICuWlD1wKx.key_idea: Take a whole multi-stage project as the evaluation unit, with timeline-released feedback and cross-file acceptance rubrics, so process quality and final delivery are scored separately.
ICuWlD1wKx.evidence: Seven model-harness systems evaluated on 11 projects and 150 subtasks.
ICuWlD1wKx.claimed_gains: Mean final-delivery scores range from 34.9 to 65.0 out of 100 and subtask pass rates at a 90-point threshold range from 12.7% to 48.7%, with every system's final-delivery score below its process score.

F4NnjP1eOQ.one_liner: Causal video diffusion without a bidirectional teacher: predict each chunk without history, then let history add only a residual.
F4NnjP1eOQ.problem: Causal video diffusion trained on ground-truth history becomes strongly dependent on it, so errors in its own generated history propagate at inference, and common fixes need a bidirectional teacher.
F4NnjP1eOQ.method: Conditional Residual Prediction (CRP) has the model first predict the target without the condition, with the condition allowed only to add a residual on top. Applied to history, each chunk is predicted from the present as far as possible and the past supplies only what the present cannot, with the causal model trained from an image-model initialization and no bidirectional video model.
F4NnjP1eOQ.key_idea: Predict the target without the condition first and let the condition add only a residual, which reduces reliance on history in autoregressive video generation.
F4NnjP1eOQ.evidence: Controlled experiments comparing against a bidirectional baseline under the same setup (details cut off in the abstract).
F4NnjP1eOQ.claimed_gains: In controlled experiments CRP nearly closes the 6.14-point gap to a bidirectional baseline (the abstract is cut off afterward).

tJlKjJymx9.one_liner: Promptable 3D segmentation trained on VLM-built nested part hierarchies with multi-granularity matching across prediction levels.
tJlKjJymx9.problem: Single-granularity annotations limit candidate coverage and target diversity for promptable 3D segmentation, especially when proposing masks from a single click.
tJlKjJymx9.method: An automatic pipeline uses a VLM to organize existing part annotations into nested hierarchies via recursive grouping and correction, yielding the PartNeXt-XL dataset. Partita fuses low-resolution prompt-aware features with high-resolution geometric features and uses multi-granularity matching to jointly supervise predictions across levels.
tJlKjJymx9.key_idea: Supervise several granularity levels per prompt via multi-granularity matching on VLM-built nested hierarchies, instead of a single target mask per prompt.
tJlKjJymx9.evidence: Experiments on interactive segmentation, multi-granularity prediction, and automatic proposal generation.
tJlKjJymx9.claimed_gains: Claims improvements in interactive segmentation and multi-granularity prediction and competitive automatic proposal generation; no performance numbers stated.

v1s3NuStbZ.one_liner: Repurposes a pretrained video generator to jointly predict future proprioception and a scalar value for robot RL.
v1s3NuStbZ.problem: Value models built on VLMs struggle to capture temporal dynamics and physical interactions, so value estimates are unreliable in long-horizon robot tasks.
v1s3NuStbZ.method: ViVa repurposes a pretrained video generator to jointly predict future proprioception and a scalar value, grounding value estimation in anticipated embodiment dynamics. It is integrated into RECAP for policy improvement.
v1s3NuStbZ.key_idea: Ground value estimation in a video generator's predictions of future proprioception, coupling value with foresight of embodiment dynamics.
v1s3NuStbZ.evidence: Metric-based evaluation across three tasks, plus integration into RECAP for robot manipulation; further settings are not stated.
v1s3NuStbZ.claimed_gains: Claims top results in metric-based evaluation across three tasks and an average success rate of 80% when integrated into RECAP.

gqqhaDr6yQ.one_liner: Models homogeneous and heterogeneous neighbors as low- and high-frequency graph signals and fuses them for multi-label node classification.
gqqhaDr6yQ.problem: Existing multi-label node classification methods suppress heterogeneous neighbors, while aggregating them causes feature entanglement and inconsistent prediction gradients among neighbors.
gqqhaDr6yQ.method: DF^2Net treats homogeneous neighborhood information as low-frequency and heterogeneous information as high-frequency signals, and applies a dual-frequency fusion strategy to exploit their complementarity. The available abstract is cut off while introducing a further Joint component.
gqqhaDr6yQ.key_idea: Split neighborhood information into low- and high-frequency components and fuse them, so heterogeneous neighbors add discriminative signal instead of being suppressed.
gqqhaDr6yQ.evidence: Not stated in the available abstract text, which is truncated.

AJ5j74TpTA.one_liner: Induces a latent hypergraph over keypoints to model group-wise structure for category-agnostic pose estimation.
AJ5j74TpTA.problem: Existing category-agnostic pose estimation methods rely on pairwise graphs, which cannot explicitly represent group-wise structures formed jointly by multiple semantic keypoints.
AJ5j74TpTA.method: HyperCape induces a latent hypergraph from contextualized keypoint representations and sparsely assigns each keypoint to a subset of latent hyperedges. The hypergraph supports feature exchange within groups and guides coordinate refinement through the relative geometry of keypoints in each hyperedge.
AJ5j74TpTA.key_idea: Sparse assignment of keypoints to latent hyperedges, used both for feature exchange and for relative-geometry coordinate refinement.
AJ5j74TpTA.evidence: Experiments on the MP-100 benchmark against graph-based CAPE methods, plus qualitative analysis of learned hyperedges on unseen categories.
AJ5j74TpTA.claimed_gains: Gains of 1.04%p in mPCK and 2.05%p at PCK@0.05 over the strongest prior method on MP-100.

5EplIxej4s.one_liner: Adds motion chain-of-thought state-transition tokens to World Action Models to decouple motion semantics from trajectory generation.
5EplIxej4s.problem: Visual branches of World Action Models predict static observations, entangling high-level physical state evolution with low-level action trajectory generation inside the Action Model.
5EplIxej4s.method: PILOT's Representational Deduction makes the action branch model potential state transition tokens, which are retained as a chain-of-thought in the reasoning space to guide fine-grained motion trajectories.
5EplIxej4s.key_idea: The action branch predicts state-transition tokens that are kept as a motion chain-of-thought guiding trajectory generation.
5EplIxej4s.evidence: Complex robotic manipulation experiments reported to improve success rate, generalization and interpretability; specific benchmarks are not stated in the available abstract.

kPEEeI2Jo1.one_liner: Unreal Engine 5 benchmark testing world-model consistency across distinct histories that reach the same state.
kPEEeI2Jo1.problem: Evaluations of video world models cover visual fidelity, control adherence and within-rollout revisit consistency, but not agreement across different histories reaching the same reference state.
kPEEeI2Jo1.method: Builds a dataset of 11,377 exploration and relation-structured videos with action and camera-pose annotations, whose trajectories form rooted graphs with shared initial states. Inverse, Loop and Equivalence tests separate self-consistency from reference fidelity and add layout and geometry readouts.
kPEEeI2Jo1.key_idea: Relation-structured trajectories with shared initial states test retracing, loop return and cross-path equivalence separately from reference fidelity.
kPEEeI2Jo1.evidence: Evaluation of nine world-model configurations on static Unreal Engine 5 scenes.

WLQIFZs0pZ.one_liner: Spectral simplicial wavelet transform with scale-selecting experts for brain connectome analysis of neurodegeneration.
WLQIFZs0pZ.problem: GNNs for brain networks focus mainly on node-level features and overlook edge-level interactions, and many spectral GNNs use fixed-bandwidth filtering that misses diverse frequency components.
WLQIFZs0pZ.method: Combines a Spectral Simplicial Wavelet Transform (SSWT) for node and edge features with a Scale-aware eXpert (ScaleX) on the simplicial complex that dynamically selects the most relevant wavelet scales for each graph.
WLQIFZs0pZ.key_idea: Per-graph selection of wavelet scales by experts over a spectral decomposition of a simplicial complex covering both nodes and edges.
WLQIFZs0pZ.evidence: Experiments on benchmark brain network datasets (not named) evaluating classification and interpretability.

D0VQmBqnwl.one_liner: Learns humanoid policies by refining imperfect motion references into feasible reference tubes using policy rollouts and a feasibility critic.
D0VQmBqnwl.problem: Video-derived motion references contain artifacts such as foot skating, ground penetration and inconsistent contacts, and joint-level tracking rewards make policies copy artifacts or chase infeasible targets.
D0VQmBqnwl.method: SetMimic estimates uncertainty to build a structured Motion Intent Representation, then samples and refines intent-consistent trajectories into a reference tube using short policy rollouts and a learned feasibility critic. An uncertainty-conditioned set-tracking objective tracks reliable components precisely.
D0VQmBqnwl.key_idea: Track only the reliable parts of an imperfect reference precisely and let robot execution feedback resolve uncertain details inside a reference tube.
D0VQmBqnwl.evidence: Not stated in the available abstract text, which is truncated.

9gqR3EvhUy.one_liner: Differentiable kinematic routing through a hierarchical ontology to score and explain differences between two performers' actions.
9gqR3EvhUy.problem: Existing methods evaluate individual performance but cannot compare two similar actions by different performers and explain how the actions differ.
9gqR3EvhUy.method: Introduces the Unified Action Difference Reasoning task and an ADR dataset built on Ego-Exo4D with paired videos, scores and language descriptions of differences. Structured Kinematic Routing finds a visual trajectory through a hierarchical kinematic ontology, regularizes paths with expert-commentary grounding, and captures counterfactual topological deviations.
9gqR3EvhUy.key_idea: Route visual features through a hierarchical kinematic ontology and regularize the paths with cross-modal grounding from expert commentary priors.
9gqR3EvhUy.evidence: A new ADR dataset built on Ego-Exo4D; experimental results are not stated in the available abstract.

fIQcelpumC.one_liner: Trains zero-shot RGB VLA policies for deformable manipulation entirely in simulation using ISP-aware photometric augmentation.
fIQcelpumC.problem: RGB sim-to-real transfer for deformable manipulation has remained largely unsolved without real-world fine-tuning.
fIQcelpumC.method: SimWeaver combines a measurement-backed simulator, a single-image asset-generation framework, a deterministic topology-aware trajectory synthesizer, and a sim-to-real protocol with ISP-aware photometric augmentation. Policies train on 200 simulated demonstrations per task.
fIQcelpumC.key_idea: Pair a measurement-backed simulator and topology-aware trajectory synthesis with ISP-aware photometric augmentation to close the RGB sim-to-real gap.
fIQcelpumC.evidence: Real-world tests on 5 deformable tasks including plastic-bag manipulation, and silk grasping under visual distribution shifts against real-data baselines.
fIQcelpumC.claimed_gains: Above 80% per-task and 91% average real-world success across 5 tasks, and 100% on silk grasping under visual shifts where real-data baselines drop to 9-70%.

s7UrVZ0Of3.one_liner: Decomposes neural basis coefficients into a boundary lift and nullspace coordinates, reprojecting state each step for moving-boundary PDEs.
s7UrVZ0Of3.problem: Boundary treatments in neural solvers for moving-boundary multiphysics problems trade off constraint accuracy against update cost.
s7UrVZ0Of3.method: NOVA splits neural basis coefficients into a boundary lift and a component in instantaneous nullspace coordinates, then reprojects the previous physical state onto the updated nullspace. It derives horizontal transport equations for the nullspace basis on the Stiefel manifold to avoid per-step SVDs, and a spectral rank-saturation criterion for boundary collocation.
s7UrVZ0Of3.key_idea: Evolve the nullspace basis by transport on the Stiefel manifold instead of recomputing SVDs, and reproject the previous state onto it.
s7UrVZ0Of3.evidence: Eight multiphysics benchmarks covering phase change and flow, multiphase flow, and free boundary problems.
s7UrVZ0Of3.claimed_gains: No numbers stated; claims best or competitive field accuracy and substantially lower boundary errors than baselines on eight benchmarks.

zeUVJ3fy0y.one_liner: Training-free routing that refuses questions with contradicted visual premises and otherwise re-answers with detector-grounded evidence.
zeUVJ3fy0y.problem: LVLMs give unreliable responses both when a question presupposes visual conditions that do not hold and when the answer adds unsupported content.
zeUVJ3fy0y.method: PAVER treats required question premises as validity checks and draft-mentioned entities only as guides for targeted visual inspection, with Grounding DINO and Florence-2 supplying shared visual evidence. A router selects refusal when a required premise is contradicted and evidence-grounded re-answering otherwise.
zeUVJ3fy0y.key_idea: Asymmetric roles for evidence: question premises decide whether to refuse, while draft entities only direct targeted visual inspection.
zeUVJ3fy0y.evidence: Six benchmarks and two LVLM backbones, with factorized ablations of the draft-guided and premise-modeling pathways.

cdXQV0nk5I.one_liner: Measures how much of the benefit of re-executing layer blocks survives the post-training stages of multimodal LLMs.
cdXQV0nk5I.problem: Latent-depth recursion methods were evaluated only on pretrained or instruction-tuned LLMs, so it is unknown whether the recursive structure survives the full multimodal post-training pipeline.
cdXQV0nk5I.method: Defines a recursion budget, the fraction of instances the default forward pass gets wrong but some recursion route gets right, computed by exhaustively evaluating every route in a small closed recursion family. It tracks this budget across training stages of several LLM and MLLM families.
cdXQV0nk5I.key_idea: Recursion budget: the share of instances where some layer-repeat route fixes a wrong default forward pass, tracked across training stages.
cdXQV0nk5I.evidence: Exhaustive route evaluation across training stages of several LLM and MLLM families; the available abstract is truncated.

LKQ4con2iF.one_liner: Benchmark scoring LLM agents' hazardous mutation designs against wet-lab measurements in a multi-round, tool-augmented setting.
LKQ4con2iF.problem: Existing biosecurity evaluations test possession of hazardous knowledge rather than practical design ability, overlook risk amplification from biological design tools, and rely on unreliable, costly or hazardous validation.
LKQ4con2iF.method: DRYLAB-Bench gives agents 30 hazardous mutation-design scenarios distilled from biosecurity guidelines in a multi-round environment where LLMs orchestrate biological design tools. Submitted designs are scored against 187,695 empirical wet-lab measurements including ProteinGym.
LKQ4con2iF.key_idea: Score agent-submitted mutation designs directly against existing empirical wet-lab measurements instead of unreliable or hazardous validation.
LKQ4con2iF.evidence: 30 scenarios scored against 187,695 measurements; the TL;DR reports that frontier models generate high-risk mutations and that design tools increase risk.

4Z2UegYSL2.one_liner: Training-free Omni-LLM compression that consolidates redundant audio-visual tokens and allocates KV-cache value precision by semantic sensitivity.
