PpOI7Udsps.method: TALA uses victim feedback to adapt perturbation location, extent, and type, combining guided patch-center sampling, failure-aware penalties, and entropy-based patch sizing. Shared rejection feedback coordinates spatial search and switching between smooth and high-frequency perturbations.
PpOI7Udsps.key_idea: Use victim localization feedback to adapt patch sampling and size while switching perturbation engines after rejection.
PpOI7Udsps.evidence: Evaluations cover three heterogeneous detectors, five datasets, and four evaluation conditions, but the supplied abstract truncates the quantitative result.

BFKPxCIp6G.one_liner: Agent watermarking supports black-box ownership verification of repackaged agents while preserving normal task functionality.
BFKPxCIp6G.problem: API-based agent repackaging can hide ownership and modify execution, while existing watermarks can disrupt agent decisions or lose recoverability.
BFKPxCIp6G.method: LoRo-Mark proposes agent watermarking intended to preserve functionality and retain ownership evidence after partial execution modification; the supplied abstract ends before its construction.

KlG2mxbSQ8.one_liner: Explicit proof obligations and intermediate logical judgments provide global and local reinforcement signals for reasoning traces.
KlG2mxbSQ8.problem: Outcome-only supervision misses invalid steps inside correct answers and valid intermediate reasoning inside incorrect responses.
KlG2mxbSQ8.method: VeriLogic decomposes reasoning into intermediate judgments, proofs, and final decisions with formally checkable obligations. Structured policy optimization combines verifier-derived global and local rewards to train both overall outcomes and intermediate reasoning.
KlG2mxbSQ8.key_idea: Expose intermediate logical judgments as checkable proof obligations and use verifier feedback for global and local policy rewards.

jllPCIV3UN.one_liner: Maps text and visual features into a shared sparse autoencoder space to build turn-level latent multimodal memory graphs.
jllPCIV3UN.problem: Flat cross-modal memory methods prematurely compress visual evidence, struggle with temporally stale observations, and make fine-grained multimodal reasoning across sessions computationally prohibitive.
jllPCIV3UN.method: LMMR maps textual hidden states and visual patch features into a shared Sparse Autoencoder concept space, using sparse activations as semantic addresses to dynamically construct a turn-level multimodal memory graph. A graph encoder aggregates cross-modal and temporal dependencies across a task-specific latent subgraph and injects the readout as a continuous residual rollout into the generation backbone while retaining native visual tokens.
jllPCIV3UN.key_idea: Index text hidden states and visual patches via shared Sparse Autoencoder activations to dynamically build and encode a latent multimodal memory graph injected into generation.
jllPCIV3UN.evidence: Evaluated on nine Mem-Gallery tasks and twelve MemEye settings (abstract truncated before results).

tXenu0gfDT.one_liner: Internalizes verified agent failure corrections into frozen vision-language-action policies via iterative conditional low-rank adaptation and a local controller.
tXenu0gfDT.problem: Online reasoning agents can assist vision-language-action policies during deployment failures, but such assistance leaves the underlying policy unchanged and dependent on repeated online reasoning.
tXenu0gfDT.method: Learning to Recover (L2R) constructs and verifies agent corrections at natural policy failures, then performs lightweight offline updates via conditional low-rank adaptation of a frozen VLA paired with a lightweight local controller to learn valid corrective actions and when to invoke them. Subsequent rounds target failures of the updated policy to track its changing behavior.
tXenu0gfDT.key_idea: Selectively adapt a frozen VLA and lightweight local controller via iterative conditional LoRA on verified agent failure corrections rather than imitating full intervention records.
tXenu0gfDT.evidence: Evaluated on ten VLABench task families across five tracks, ten RoboDojo tasks, and three real-world robotic manipulation tasks.
tXenu0gfDT.claimed_gains: One round trained on in-distribution corrections achieves 52.0% conditional recovery on ten VLABench task families versus 31.8% for standard LoRA, while three rounds improve policy-only success from 12.6% to 27.4% on ten RoboDojo tasks and from 33.3% to 68.3% on three real-world tasks.

uVwuqLwFRC.one_liner: Logs per-step physics states and replays solver perturbations to audit false contact artifacts in simulated robot benchmarks.
uVwuqLwFRC.problem: Simulated robot benchmarks penalize policies for failed episodes in which the physics simulator ejects already placed objects due to collision-detection artifacts.
uVwuqLwFRC.method: SimuGuard is an auditing plugin that records per-step physics states, flags objects accelerating at contact faster than robot contact or gravity explain, and replays episodes bit-for-bit alongside single-parameter solver changes. Using this diagnostic, the authors trace object-ejection failures to a fixed PhysX collision-detection threshold reporting roughly two-centimeter overlaps with thin container walls.
uVwuqLwFRC.key_idea: Flag physically unexplained contact velocities at every simulation step and replay recorded episodes under modified solver parameters to isolate false collision-detection overlaps.
uVwuqLwFRC.evidence: Tested over ten vision-language-action and world-action models across five benchmarks (LIBERO, RoboTwin, RoboCasa, RoboDojo, and RoboLab), plus real-robot ranking comparisons across five models.
uVwuqLwFRC.claimed_gains: With a smaller collision threshold, LingBot-VA succeeds in 98 of 100 episodes versus 89 with zero contact artifacts, and model rankings across five models match real-robot rankings.

Yljsbxj26I.one_liner: Recursively partitions variables using d-separating shields to learn local Bayesian network subgraphs in parallel before merging residual dependencies.
Yljsbxj26I.problem: Bayesian network structure learning scales poorly with the number of variables due to costly conditional-independence testing and graph search.
Yljsbxj26I.method: Shield-Induced Partitioning (SIP) uses a seed-and-expand procedure to decompose variables into two main blocks and a shield split into a conditioning component that d-separates the blocks and a residual component. Independent structure learning is performed on smaller local domains combining each block with the conditioning shield, followed by a merge step that recovers residual shield-mediated dependencies.
Yljsbxj26I.key_idea: Decompose variables into d-separated blocks via a split conditioning-and-residual shield so local subgraphs can be learned independently and merged.
Yljsbxj26I.evidence: Supported by theoretical P-map class recovery guarantees under Markov and faithfulness assumptions and experiments on discrete Bayesian-network benchmarks against structure-learning baselines.

y8fVaDC7vK.one_liner: Benchmarks coding agents on full-stack training and inference optimization across multi-accelerator GPU and NPU clusters via OCI layers.
y8fVaDC7vK.problem: Existing agent-driven optimization benchmarks target isolated software layers rather than evaluating end-to-end training and inference speedups under production workloads.
y8fVaDC7vK.method: RSIBench-Infra provides 20 runnable training and inference baselines across diverse model families and modalities on up to 32 NVIDIA GPUs and Ascend NPUs, allowing agents to modify engine, kernel, and instruction layers. Modifications are captured via an OCI image-layer submission protocol for reproducible deployment and evaluated on end-to-end performance under task-specific quality constraints.
y8fVaDC7vK.key_idea: Package agent edits across engine, kernel, and instruction layers as reproducible OCI image layers and measure quality-constrained end-to-end speedups on multi-accelerator deployments.
y8fVaDC7vK.evidence: Evaluated across six agent-model configurations and 120 trials over 20 training and inference tasks deployed on up to 32 NVIDIA GPUs and Ascend NPUs.
y8fVaDC7vK.claimed_gains: Across six agent-model configurations and 120 trials, 57 trials achieve validated speedups above 1.10x, with the top configuration exceeding 1.10x on 60% of tasks.

0SqlacvM6k.one_liner: Forecasts time series via random-order autoregressive generation over visual series images trained with coupled teacher-forcing and free-running supervision.
0SqlacvM6k.problem: Existing autoregressive time-series forecasters are constrained by rigid sequential generation orders and suffer from exposure bias and error accumulation.
0SqlacvM6k.method: ROAR represents time series visually and reformulates forecasting as a random-order autoregressive generation task over the time-series image. It trains the backbone with a coupled supervision strategy combining signals from both teacher-forcing and free-running rollouts to reduce training-inference mismatch.
0SqlacvM6k.key_idea: Formulate time-series forecasting as random-order autoregressive generation on rendered time-series images under joint teacher-forcing and free-running supervision.
0SqlacvM6k.evidence: Evaluated across 10 real-world time-series forecasting benchmarks across multiple domains.

P9qGwc6an8.one_liner: Uses unbiased CKA and frozen-predictor sensitive subspace analysis to compare cross-species auditory cortex encoding across pretraining domains.
P9qGwc6an8.problem: Whether deep neural network generalization in predicting auditory neural responses extends across species-specific pretraining domains such as human speech versus animal vocalizations remains unclear.
P9qGwc6an8.method: The authors evaluate self-supervised and supervised audio models pretrained on corpora spanning human speech to animal vocalizations on animal and human neural response prediction tasks. They apply unbiased Centered Kernel Alignment (uCKA) to model activations and introduce a sensitive subspace analysis on frozen encoding predictors to determine whether pretraining-domain input geometry persists in neural readouts.
P9qGwc6an8.key_idea: Combine activation-level unbiased Centered Kernel Alignment with sensitive subspace analysis of frozen encoding predictors to test where pretraining-domain geometry survives cross-species neural readout.
P9qGwc6an8.evidence: Tested self-supervised and supervised audio models pretrained across human speech and animal vocalization corpora on animal and human auditory neural response prediction datasets.

YhBU3srcAn.one_liner: Post-trains multimodal LLMs with counterfactual visual-region gates and GRPO-decoupled proper confidence losses for visually traceable confidence calibration.
YhBU3srcAn.problem: Binary-correctness calibration objectives calibrate answer probabilities without verifying whether specific visual evidence warrants the reported confidence.
YhBU3srcAn.method: TraceConf post-trains multimodal LLMs to jointly generate declared visual evidence regions, an answer, and a confidence choice while counterfactually removing and isolating declared regions to compute a necessity-and-sufficiency evidence gate. The gate rewards grounded responses and weights a local proper confidence loss, while excluding the confidence-choice token from the shared sequence-level GRPO advantage.
YhBU3srcAn.key_idea: Weight a local proper confidence loss with a counterfactual region necessity-and-sufficiency gate while excluding the confidence token from shared sequence-level GRPO advantages.
YhBU3srcAn.evidence: Evaluated across six multimodal benchmarks on confidence calibration and error discrimination.

ZVbv5AjKGu.one_liner: Modulates the amplitude spectrum of distribution-matching distillation updates to suppress dominant low-frequency error tails during few-step diffusion training.
ZVbv5AjKGu.problem: Low-frequency spectral amplitudes dominate the directional error field in Distribution Matching Distillation, overwhelming mid- and high-frequency signals and slowing fine-detail recovery.
ZVbv5AjKGu.method: Spectral Amplitude Purification for Distribution Matching Distillation (SAP-DMD) adaptively suppresses the dominant low-frequency tail of the amplitude spectrum in DMD directional updates as a plug-and-play training modification.
ZVbv5AjKGu.key_idea: Suppress extreme low-frequency spectral amplitudes in the distribution-matching directional field so mid- and high-frequency details receive stronger distillation signal.
ZVbv5AjKGu.evidence: Evaluated on PixArt-alpha, SD3, and SD3.5 under 2-step and 4-step diffusion sampling.

1CCnjFvXkC.one_liner: Certifies globally optimal maximum-consensus SO(3) rotation averaging by solving bracketing integer Markov random fields via adaptive branch-and-bound subdivision.
1CCnjFvXkC.problem: Heuristic robust rotation-averaging solvers provide no optimality certificates, while existing certifiable relaxations only certify least-squares surrogates that break down under heavy outlier contamination.
1CCnjFvXkC.method: The method covers SO(3) with certified-radius cells to bound the NP-hard maximum-consensus objective between two integer Markov random fields (cell-center decoding from below and radius-inflated satisfiability from above) and solves both simultaneously via adaptive branch-and-bound subdivision.
1CCnjFvXkC.key_idea: Cover SO(3) with certified-radius cells to form lower- and upper-bounding integer Markov random fields solved jointly via branch-and-bound subdivision.
1CCnjFvXkC.evidence: Proves finite-resolution bracket closure determined by the instance margin and evaluates runtime and accuracy across outlier rates up to 90% on synthetic rotation graphs.
1CCnjFvXkC.claimed_gains: On synthetic graphs, the optimality bracket closes on every instance in about one minute, achieving the highest accuracy across all tested outlier rates and remaining functional at 90% outliers.

ZczSdKgGKU.one_liner: Decomposes path-integrated feature gradients into parent-explained and residual movements along known causal graphs to separate direct and mediated attributions.
ZczSdKgGKU.problem: Dependency-aware feature attribution methods like causal Shapley values fail to scale to high dimensions, while standard integrated gradients credit correlated downstream descendants over upstream causal drivers.
ZczSdKgGKU.method: Causal Integrated Gradients (CIG) and Causal Expected Gradients (CEG) incorporate a known input causal graph by splitting each feature's differential movement along the integration path into variation explained by its causal parents and its own residual, separating direct and mediated effects.
ZczSdKgGKU.key_idea: Split each feature's movement along the gradient integration path into variation explained by its causal parents and its independent residual.
ZczSdKgGKU.evidence: Analyzed for axiomatic guarantees and evaluated against Pearl's do-calculus ground truth and causal Shapley values on synthetic causal benchmarks and simulated single-cell gene expression data.

wjl0Mcjw6V.one_liner: Trains deepfake detectors with an H-consistent bi-level balanced loss addressing both class-level and domain-level data imbalances.
wjl0Mcjw6V.problem: Existing deepfake detectors either ignore class imbalance or handle class ratios alone while overlooking domain-level imbalance and sample hardness across diverse manipulation sources.
wjl0Mcjw6V.method: The paper formulates bi-level imbalanced deepfake detection and introduces a bi-level balanced training loss backed by general H-consistency and special-case Bayes consistency guarantees.
wjl0Mcjw6V.key_idea: Formulate a bi-level balanced classification loss with H-consistency guarantees to jointly reweight class-level and domain-level imbalances alongside sample hardness.
wjl0Mcjw6V.evidence: Supported by H-consistency and Bayes-consistency proofs and empirical comparisons against existing losses across multiple DNN deepfake detector backbones.

WnjTjdaBXP.one_liner: Spectral anchoring and cross-domain rectification adapt CLIP across domains without training.
WnjTjdaBXP.problem: Existing CLIP-based multi-domain learning relies on heavy architectures and complex training rather than fully exploiting pretrained priors.
WnjTjdaBXP.method: STAR uses Subspace Anchor Guidance to preserve dominant class-domain spectral structure while suppressing nuisance-sensitive tail directions. CrOss-domain REctification adds complementary cross-domain evidence when compatible with self-domain Gaussian geometry.
WnjTjdaBXP.key_idea: Suppress spectral-tail nuisance directions and rectify self-domain predictions using Gaussian-compatible cross-domain spectral evidence.
WnjTjdaBXP.evidence: Spectral and Gaussian-geometric analyses identify domain-dependent class geometry, spectral-tail nuisance variation, and cross-domain recoverability associated with self-domain geometry.

bv2AQntxRX.one_liner: Continuous implicit scene representations reconstruct coherent geometry and appearance from unposed multi-view images.
bv2AQntxRX.problem: Explicit pixel-aligned pointmap regression in visual geometry models introduces redundancy and limits geometric continuity.
bv2AQntxRX.method: IVGT learns a continuous neural scene representation in canonical coordinates and retrieves local features at arbitrary 3D queries. Lightweight decoders predict signed distances and colors, supporting surface extraction, rendering, and pose-free reconstruction.
bv2AQntxRX.key_idea: Query a canonical implicit scene field at continuous 3D positions to decode signed distance and color instead of regressing pointmaps.
bv2AQntxRX.evidence: Multi-dataset joint training with 2D supervision and 3D regularization is evaluated on reconstruction, novel-view synthesis, depth, normals, and camera pose estimation.

PYMneorGsY.one_liner: Retained block attention predicts dropped contributions for efficient sparse video diffusion.
PYMneorGsY.problem: Block-wise sparse attention is efficient but coarse, while centroid-wise masks are adaptive but require costly irregular computation.
PYMneorGsY.method: RDA combines recovery-aware top-p block selection with compensation that predicts dropped contributions from retained attention outputs. A sensitivity-driven scheduler assigns top-p settings across denoising steps and layers under a calibrated attention-error objective and sparsity budget.
PYMneorGsY.key_idea: Estimate discarded attention contributions from already-computed retained blocks and schedule recovery by layer-step sensitivity.
PYMneorGsY.evidence: Experiments on 720p HunyuanVideo and Wan2.1 compare sparse-baseline fidelity and measure speedups at fixed sparsity levels.
PYMneorGsY.claimed_gains: RDA achieves 2.010× and 1.663× speedups at 78.3% and 77.1% sparsity on 720p HunyuanVideo and Wan2.1, respectively.

nZmCdkGowC.one_liner: Coupled-axis relation prompts adapt compact attention aggregation to instance-specific image degradations.
nZmCdkGowC.problem: All-in-one restoration must organize attention responses and their interactions adaptively for unknown heterogeneous degradations.
nZmCdkGowC.method: InCaRP constructs compact K/V carriers through low-rank relation-space attention and composes query-axis and relation-axis prompts via shared hyperspherical retrieval. Normalized prompt interactions produce bounded scale and shift fields, while spatial value reweighting localizes restoration effects.
nZmCdkGowC.key_idea: Compose paired query-axis and relation-axis prompts through hyperspherical retrieval to calibrate low-rank attention logits per instance.
nZmCdkGowC.evidence: Experiments on all-in-one and real-world benchmarks evaluate balanced restoration, unseen-degradation generalization, parameter counts, and FLOPs.

TZuNUA2v1u.one_liner: Full-cycle benchmarks evaluate environment reconstruction, implementation, and test generation by autonomous code agents.
TZuNUA2v1u.problem: Preconfigured environments and rigid static evaluation pipelines hide practical friction and misjudge fully autonomous issue-resolution trajectories.
TZuNUA2v1u.method: SWE-Cycle provides 489 filtered instances across environment reconstruction, code implementation, verification test generation, and an integrated FullCycle task. SWE-Judge combines static code review with dynamic testing to assess execution-capable functional correctness.
TZuNUA2v1u.key_idea: Carry one agent's environment, code, tests, and session state through the complete issue-resolution cycle from a bare repository.
TZuNUA2v1u.evidence: Code agents powered by seven LLMs are evaluated across four tasks, revealing lower solve rates in FullCycle than in isolated tasks.

YeXFpZL85v.one_liner: Uses concept-conditioned semantic attention during training for fine-grained audio-text retrieval while reducing to a dual encoder at inference.
YeXFpZL85v.problem: Fine-grained audio-text retrieval either relies on fixed frame-level event taxonomies or incurs multi-prototype similarity overhead at inference.
YeXFpZL85v.method: SAYAKA parses captions into semantic concepts, queries shared audio tokens via semantic attention, applies soft-positive alignment and concept separation losses, and fuses representations via adaptive recomposition into a standard dual encoder.
YeXFpZL85v.key_idea: Trains with concept-queried semantic attention and soft-positive separation losses, collapsing to a single-vector dual encoder at inference.

UyZmmvlJAC.one_liner: Learns task-relevant features and aligns them across viewpoints using a FiLM network conditioned on predicted camera rotation.
UyZmmvlJAC.problem: Enforcing strict cross-view consistency in visual robotic manipulation can discard viewpoint-dependent task-relevant information.
UyZmmvlJAC.method: RCA first learns task-relevant representations from observations, then adapts and aligns them across viewpoints in a unified latent space via a FiLM mapping network conditioned on predicted viewpoint parameters.
UyZmmvlJAC.key_idea: Conditions cross-view feature alignment on predicted camera rotation parameters via FiLM after extracting task-relevant visual representations.
UyZmmvlJAC.evidence: Evaluations in Meta-World and PandaGym simulations and real-world robot manipulation experiments under viewpoint perturbations.
UyZmmvlJAC.claimed_gains: Improves average success rates over baselines by 19.8, 26.7, 4.2, and 6.9 percentage points in Meta-World azimuth, Meta-World camera shaking, PandaGym azimuth, and real-world azimuth evaluations.

d1haddFStx.one_liner: Proposes RTR, a post-hoc graph unlearning method using node-interaction reconstruction and range-null-space rectification.
d1haddFStx.problem: Approximate graph unlearning often requires partial retraining, full-parameter re-estimation, or costly influence approximations.
d1haddFStx.method: Keeping base GNN parameters fixed, RTR estimates node interactions via information-conserving reconstruction, refines them with range-null-space decomposition under a linear inverse constraint, and subtracts them from retained-node embeddings.
d1haddFStx.key_idea: Rectifies reconstructed node-interaction estimates via range-null-space decomposition before subtracting them from fixed GNN embeddings.
d1haddFStx.evidence: Theoretical L2-error non-increase guarantee and experiments across multiple datasets, four GNN backbones, poisoned-node removal, and membership inference attacks.

Y0pGvcXSbv.one_liner: Introduces ASVBench, evaluating asynchronous delayed responses to fine-grained visual triggers in streaming videos.
Y0pGvcXSbv.problem: Existing streaming video benchmarks assume immediate-query, immediate-answer interactions rather than waiting for future fine-grained visual triggers.
Y0pGvcXSbv.method: They construct ASVBench (1,452 videos, 4,350 Q&A pairs) with a dual-axis evaluation covering temporal scenarios (Immediate, Prospective, Continuous Q&A) and cognitive trigger levels.
Y0pGvcXSbv.key_idea: Evaluates delayed asynchronous responses to object-centric triggers across Immediate, Prospective, and Continuous streaming Q&A.
Y0pGvcXSbv.evidence: Benchmark dataset of 1,452 videos and 4,350 Q&A pairs.

ae4GatERdz.one_liner: Proposes Maglev, decomposing recommenders into hardware-local pipeline stages with learned indexers, low-rank residuals, and bubble-free scheduling.
ae4GatERdz.problem: Industrial recommenders face diminishing returns from dense scaling while global feature interaction and distributed training make sparse and depth scaling expensive.
ae4GatERdz.method: Maglev combines Maglev Indexers (capacity-bounded stage inputs), Maglev Induct (low-rank cross-stage residuals), and Maglev Rail (bubble-free pipeline schedule with synchronous gradient clipping).
ae4GatERdz.key_idea: Decomposes recommenders into hardware-local stages linked by learned indexers, low-rank residuals, and bubble-free pipeline scheduling.
ae4GatERdz.evidence: Industrial study (28B samples, 700 features, four tasks) on Wukong and DHEN, three public benchmarks across five backbones, and KuaiVideo with HSTU and OneTrans-style backbones.
ae4GatERdz.claimed_gains: Trains up to 1.3x faster than hybrid parallelism and improves five additional backbones across all 15 matched-compute settings on three public benchmarks.

6NOMPVMb9o.one_liner: Introduces WideUAV benchmark and UNISAG model for joint wide-area satellite-tile retrieval and target-extent grounding.
6NOMPVMb9o.problem: Existing cross-view benchmarks crop tightly around targets, neglecting the combined challenge of retrieving wide satellite tiles and grounding off-center targets from UAV views.
6NOMPVMb9o.method: They build WideUAV (3,505 tiles of 2370m x 1328m, 112,160 UAV queries across altitudes and headings) and propose UNISAG, sharing visual features across retrieval and grounding with heading/altitude cues.
6NOMPVMb9o.key_idea: Unifies satellite retrieval and bounding-box grounding in one representation conditioned on UAV altitude and heading, scored by retrieval-gated uIoU.
6NOMPVMb9o.evidence: Evaluated on WideUAV using retrieval-gated uIoU against re-implemented baselines including TransGeo.
6NOMPVMb9o.claimed_gains: UNISAG achieves 22.67% retrieval-gated uIoU on WideUAV, an 18.87-point gain over the compared baseline.

XUwndWpyMe.one_liner: Branches deterministic flow-matching steps into stochastic SDE rollouts to self-distill step-wise velocity updates without a teacher.
XUwndWpyMe.problem: On-policy distillation for flow matching requires training expensive task-specific teachers and suffers from teacher-student distribution mismatch.
XUwndWpyMe.method: Self-OPD branches each deterministic next-state prediction into K stochastic SDE candidates, rolls them out with an ODE sampler, and scores them against a deterministic self-reference baseline. It optimizes the velocity field with an all-branch pull-push objective using direction-aware attenuation, SDE-variance normalization, and reward-level multi-objective fusion.
XUwndWpyMe.key_idea: Branching deterministic states into K SDE rollouts scored against a self-reference baseline provides teacher-free step-wise pull-push velocity supervision.
XUwndWpyMe.evidence: Experiments evaluate Self-OPD on single-reward and mixed-reward flow-matching alignment benchmarks.

I7alsfMYbO.one_liner: Enforces trajectory-proxy constraints in video diffusion via irreversible gate admission, one-sided Jacobian cone projection, and nonlinear guards.
I7alsfMYbO.problem: In reverse diffusion sampling, later denoising updates violate earlier satisfied constraints while premature enforcement blocks unmet constraints.
I7alsfMYbO.method: Certified Constraint Lifecycles (CCL) admits constraints irreversibly once observer-supported satisfaction holds, projects subsequent sampler proposals onto a one-sided Jacobian cone, and applies a finite-step nonlinear endpoint guard.
I7alsfMYbO.key_idea: Tracks an admission-preservation lifecycle that irreversibly protects satisfied trajectory-proxy constraints via one-sided Jacobian cone projection and nonlinear guards.
I7alsfMYbO.evidence: Proves guarded commitment invariance and exact pre-guard row-space decomposition, supported by controlled trajectory-proxy video diffusion experiments.

AaGCKaikNi.one_liner: Combines diffusion training with a Cost-Weighted Cross-Entropy loss to align distributions with stochastic discrete optimization.
AaGCKaikNi.problem: Decision-focused learning for stochastic discrete optimization faces non-differentiable decisions and objectives depending on full outcome distributions.
AaGCKaikNi.method: The authors propose Cost-Weighted Cross-Entropy (CWCE), a differentiable surrogate loss using realized downstream costs to align expected-cost profiles without differentiating through the discrete optimizer, and combine it with diffusion training.
AaGCKaikNi.key_idea: Uses realized downstream costs to weight a differentiable cross-entropy surrogate alongside diffusion training so excess risk bounds decision regret.
AaGCKaikNi.evidence: Theoretical regret-control theorems and experiments on three stochastic discrete optimization tasks.

PeAjx9FpDq.one_liner: Stores agent memory as an operation ledger and executes writes at recall time to produce verifiable access certificates.
PeAjx9FpDq.problem: Text-retrieval agent memories cannot reliably track updates, deletions, temporal validity, or principal-level access permissions.
PeAjx9FpDq.method: TRACE records each memory write as an operation (add, replace, delete) in a ledger and executes the ledger at recall time for the requested timestamp and principal, outputting structured answers paired with verification certificates explaining included and excluded facts.
PeAjx9FpDq.key_idea: Models agent memory recall as deterministic execution over an operation ledger, emitting verifiable certificates for temporal validity and access exclusions.
PeAjx9FpDq.evidence: Formal determinism proofs and evaluations on fixed ledgers and AutoMemoryBench against dense-reader and full-lifecycle vendor baselines.
PeAjx9FpDq.claimed_gains: On fixed ledgers all 659 recalls are admissible with 0.00 misuse (vs. 0.238-0.826 for a dense reader) and all 435 certificates verify; on AutoMemoryBench, TRACE succeeds on 4.0% of cases vs. at most 0.1% for vendors.

nxVNjtx9cD.one_liner: Models text instructions as text graphs and applies unified multi-order covariance operators with asymmetric masking for cross-domain graph-text transfer.
nxVNjtx9cD.problem: Input feature heterogeneity across domains and topological distortion from graph serialization limit cross-domain and cross-modal transfer in graph foundation models.
nxVNjtx9cD.method: UniCO represents natural language instructions as text graphs, casting cross-domain and cross-modal learning as unified heterogeneous graph generalization. It builds multi-order covariance operators for graph-text interaction with an asymmetric mask preserving instruction order while shielding graphs from instruction noise, and proves basis-transformation invariance.
nxVNjtx9cD.key_idea: Casts text instructions as text graphs and uses basis-invariant multi-order covariance operators with asymmetric masking to unify graph-text transfer.
nxVNjtx9cD.evidence: Supported by theoretical basis-transformation invariance proofs and experiments on multiple molecular graph and text-attributed graph benchmarks.

NkcKUfePkY.one_liner: Grounds self-evolving LLM agents in Active Inference via Worker EFE action contracts and Builder VFE memory updates.
NkcKUfePkY.problem: Memory-based LLM agents learn retrospectively from observed trajectories without testing whether extracted rules can prospectively predict outcomes.
NkcKUfePkY.method: PACT-Agent represents uncertain environment dynamics as competing mechanisms in unresolved rules linked to numerical inference via predictive contracts. During interaction, a Worker predicts mechanism-conditioned traces and minimizes Expected Free Energy (EFE); afterward, a Builder minimizes Variational Free Energy (VFE), accepting memory edits only when trajectory interpretability outweighs description complexity.
NkcKUfePkY.key_idea: Connects LLM reasoning to Active Inference via predictive contracts, selecting actions by Worker EFE and accepting memory edits by Builder VFE.
NkcKUfePkY.evidence: Evaluated across multiple LLM-agent benchmarks against memory-based agent baselines.

fVEHd1is5g.one_liner: Converts game solver state-value changes into turn-level advantage signals for reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards.
fVEHd1is5g.problem: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards for long-horizon LLM agents suffers from sparse terminal rewards that obscure turn-level action credit.
fVEHd1is5g.method: CAST (Credit Assignment from Solver Teachers) computes changes in a game solver's state values across transitions, converts them into solver advantages, and injects them as turn-level signals into RLVR. Under a soft-optimal solver assumption, this matches on-policy distillation using only scalar values.
fVEHd1is5g.key_idea: Translates scalar state-value differences from a game solver into turn-level advantages injected into RLVR without requiring teacher logits.
fVEHd1is5g.evidence: Evaluated on Sokoban, Minesweeper, and Rush Hour under in-domain and unseen-difficulty splits, plus zero-shot transfer on ALFWorld and WebShop.

XOuR1btNyb.one_liner: Formalizes LLM creativity as quality on long-tail input-output pairs and introduces the q@Tail diagnostic metric.
XOuR1btNyb.problem: Diverse LLM creativity benchmarks use varying tasks and metrics, leaving unclear whether they measure a shared underlying notion of creativity.
XOuR1btNyb.method: The authors define creativity as task-specific quality in the long tail of a reference distribution, using n-gram absence from pretraining data as a novelty proxy. They introduce q@Tail(alpha) to measure mean task quality on the tail fraction of existing benchmarks.
XOuR1btNyb.key_idea: Measures LLM creativity by evaluating task quality specifically on the long-tail subset of input-output pairs identified via pretraining n-gram absence.
XOuR1btNyb.evidence: Evaluated empirically across 15 benchmarks and 26 open-weight models, comparing tail-subset rankings against human creativity judgments in LM-Arena.

ZQug0BI13I.one_liner: Retrieves shared embeddings from an Action Experience Dictionary and trains with motion-aware transition loss for world action models.
ZQug0BI13I.problem: World Action Models fail to reuse historical action experience across manipulation tasks and are distracted by redundant background elements.
ZQug0BI13I.method: The Action Experience Dictionary (AED) aggregates historical trajectories via a pretrained action tokenizer into shared action embeddings, conditions them visually via cross-attention, and prepends them to noisy action tokens. A motion-aware transition loss supervises visual feature change prediction over random temporal intervals.
ZQug0BI13I.key_idea: Retrieves cross-task action embeddings from a historical dictionary via a pretrained tokenizer and prepends them to noisy action tokens with a motion-aware transition loss.
ZQug0BI13I.evidence: Evaluated on simulation benchmarks and real-world cross-embodiment manipulation settings.

NM8W2HvbwY.one_liner: Predicts 100-Hz 3D velocity and angular rate from one-second IMU windows in one step via conditional bridge matching.
NM8W2HvbwY.problem: State-of-the-art inertial navigation regresses a single displacement per second, while dense-rate estimators lose accuracy or require iterative sampling.
NM8W2HvbwY.method: InertialBridge uses a Mamba3 state-space drift network conditioned on a frozen VAE and source IMU window, trained with a boundary-weighted scheduler and structured kinematic loss. Conditioning on the source window makes interior bridge targets algebraically identifiable for single-step prediction.
NM8W2HvbwY.key_idea: Applies conditional bridge matching with a boundary-weighted scheduler and frozen-VAE-conditioned Mamba3 drift to predict 100-Hz IMU trajectories in one evaluation.
NM8W2HvbwY.evidence: Evaluated via population analysis, a three-seed scheduling sweep, and RoNIN dataset benchmarks against EqNIO and dense estimators.
NM8W2HvbwY.claimed_gains: Predicts 100 samples in one evaluation using 1.95 M parameters and 0.87 GFLOPs per window versus 5.03 M and 0.84 GFLOPs for EqNIO; uniform scheduling yields 1.9–2.6 times the position ATE of boundary-weighted schedules.

FXsvtZWnIy.one_liner: Introduces r-msi and f-msi, subcubic hierarchical linkage algorithms aligned with the k-medians objective.
FXsvtZWnIy.problem: Existing hierarchical linkage methods aligned with the k-medians objective, such as msi, run in cubic time and lack scalability.
FXsvtZWnIy.method: The authors propose r-msi and f-msi as fast variants of the msi linkage algorithm, achieving O(n^2 log n) and O(n^2) time complexity respectively while producing inversion-free dendrograms. For weighted graphs, f-msi runs in O((m + n sqrt(m)) log m) time and also supports a gamma-approximated subquadratic variant.
FXsvtZWnIy.key_idea: Modifies msi linkage into r-msi and f-msi to achieve subcubic and quadratic time complexities with inversion-free dendrograms and fast weighted-graph variants.
FXsvtZWnIy.evidence: Supported by time-complexity proofs and experiments across multiple datasets from different domains, including large graph datasets.
FXsvtZWnIy.claimed_gains: Achieves clustering quality close to msi while being up to 75 times faster.

2rpWCg6vwi.one_liner: Reconciles the exploration conflict between fine-grained and shared MoE experts via token-adaptive suppression of unnecessary experts.
2rpWCg6vwi.problem: Shared experts reduce token representation variability and routing exploration, conflicting with the larger routing space required by fine-grained MoE segmentation.
2rpWCg6vwi.method: MirrorMoE shrinks the effective routing exploration space by applying token-adaptive suppression to unnecessary experts during pretraining.
2rpWCg6vwi.key_idea: Applies token-adaptive suppression of unnecessary experts to shrink the combinatorial routing space induced by fine-grained MoE segmentation.
2rpWCg6vwi.evidence: Pretraining experiments across multiple model scales.

uLcqi3rdO9.one_liner: Derives process rewards for SWE agents using potential differences of file exposure and asynchronous sandbox test verification.
uLcqi3rdO9.problem: Long-horizon software engineering (SWE) agents trained with outcome-only RLVR lack step-level credit assignment to separate productive edits from redundant exploration or regressions.
uLcqi3rdO9.method: SWE-MILE defines navigation and verification potentials from task-relevant file exposure and test-state alignment, propagating potential-difference credits backward to earlier steps. An asynchronous shadow probing mechanism replays repository edits in an isolated sandbox to run tests in parallel with the main agent.
uLcqi3rdO9.key_idea: Combines file-exposure and test-alignment potential differences with asynchronous sandbox replay probing to turn runtime milestones into low-latency process rewards for SWE RL.
uLcqi3rdO9.evidence: Evaluated on two representative long-horizon software engineering tasks.

vGj0HJIJq3.one_liner: Builds a 2,826-hour real-world video dataset with camera trajectories and hierarchical annotations for interactive world modeling.
vGj0HJIJq3.problem: Existing exploration video datasets rarely combine minute-scale continuity, camera trajectories, temporally grounded semantics, and explicit spatial revisit structure.
vGj0HJIJq3.method: Sekai2 re-curates Sekai footage and adds newly collected perspective and panoramic videos under a unified pipeline pairing clips with camera trajectories and hierarchical motion, scene, and camera annotations.
vGj0HJIJq3.key_idea: Pairs continuous minute-scale perspective and loop-closing panoramic videos with camera trajectories and hierarchical motion-scene-camera segment annotations.
vGj0HJIJq3.evidence: Dataset statistics totaling 128,892 clips (2,826 hours across 113 countries/regions), 649,597 segments, and 982 panoramic sequences (119 hours).

OeYN1hrBGu.one_liner: Diagnoses unsupported visual claim persistence under image intervention and attenuates positive RL credit for persistent claims.
OeYN1hrBGu.problem: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards can make vision-language models more visually sensitive overall while making unsupported visual claims more persistent.
OeYN1hrBGu.method: A fixed-rollout counterfactual diagnostic re-scores responses under intervened images to separate Evidence-Function Sensitivity from claim persistence. Persistence-Aware Credit Gating (PACG) then attenuates positive RL credit for unusually persistent visual claims.
OeYN1hrBGu.key_idea: Uses counterfactual image-intervention re-scoring to detect persistent unsupported visual claims and down-weights their positive RL credit via PACG.
OeYN1hrBGu.evidence: Evaluated on Qwen2.5-VL-7B across four multimodal reasoning benchmarks comparing DAPO, VPPO, GRPO, and PACG.
OeYN1hrBGu.claimed_gains: Before RL training, 27.81% of correctly answered Qwen2.5-VL-7B responses contain at least one unsupported direct visual claim.

fPKcAz5Yub.one_liner: Extends Modern Hopfield Networks to retrieve over continuous or sampled group quotient orbits.
fPKcAz5Yub.problem: Standard Modern Hopfield Networks retrieve over individual vectors and treat rotationally equivalent poses as separate memories.
fPKcAz5Yub.method: Group-Orbit Modern Hopfield Networks (G-MHNs) aggregate transformation evidence within each quotient orbit via a T-step update admitting both finite-sampled and continuous-Haar evaluation, with proven equivariance and orbit-invariant energy.
fPKcAz5Yub.key_idea: Aggregates transformation evidence across group orbits in a T-step Hopfield update to retrieve semantic orbit classes rather than single poses.
fPKcAz5Yub.evidence: Proves equivariance, energy invariance, and capacity certificates, and evaluates hidden-atom RMSD on official rMD17 splits.
fPKcAz5Yub.claimed_gains: Reduces hidden-atom RMSD by 10.8-22.8% relative to nearest-pose Procrustes retrieval on rMD17 and wins all 40 split-condition comparisons.

djoMVhbVZt.one_liner: Argues that single-agent AI alignment is ill-defined, unsolvable, and insufficient due to emergent risks in human-AI societies.
djoMVhbVZt.problem: AI safety research often treats alignment as a solvable, static property of individual AI models rather than an ongoing complex-systems problem.
djoMVhbVZt.method: This position paper critiques alignment on three grounds—lack of stable human values, impossibility of general solutions, and emergent interaction/feedback-loop risks in hybrid human-machine societies—and advocates continual adaptation.
djoMVhbVZt.key_idea: Frames human-AI collectives as complex adaptive systems where emergent interaction risks persist even if individual agents are aligned.
djoMVhbVZt.evidence: Conceptual and complex-systems argumentation (position paper; no empirical experiments).

Em0d3JLRPl.one_liner: Benchmarks VLM reasoning on optical experiments across 1,961 scenes and four progressive physics-grounded question levels.
Em0d3JLRPl.problem: No existing benchmark evaluates whether vision-language models can reason about optical experimental setups, measurements, and system decisions.
Em0d3JLRPl.method: OpticalBench pairs system components, poses, parameters, setup diagrams, and optical results across six optical phenomena (1,961 scenes, 31,887 images), synthesizing 7,664 QA pairs across four levels: Perception, Derivation, Prediction, and Decision.
Em0d3JLRPl.key_idea: Constructs setup-result optical pairs across six phenomena and synthesizes four-level physics-grounded QA tasks with per-item chance floors and visual ablations.
Em0d3JLRPl.evidence: Evaluates 10 proprietary and open-weight VLM deployments on 7,664 QA pairs under a unified protocol.

BfUoweZTKp.one_liner: Compares EMA, learning-rate decay, and Schedule-Free optimization for training large diffusion models.
BfUoweZTKp.problem: Large diffusion models typically rely on constant learning rates with EMA, while LR decay and Schedule-Free optimization remain underexplored.
BfUoweZTKp.method: The authors analyze constant-step trajectory averaging versus LR decay and Schedule-Free SGD through variance reduction and nonconvex stationarity bounds, and empirically compare EMA, LR decay+EMA, and Schedule-Free training.
BfUoweZTKp.key_idea: Shows constant-LR EMA has an inherent stationarity limitation whereas LR decay and Schedule-Free SGD achieve arbitrarily small stationarity bounds.
BfUoweZTKp.evidence: Nonconvex variance-reduction theory and diffusion training experiments evaluated over the 320k-400k iteration interval.

l02aE3Tujl.one_liner: Decouples LLM reasoning exploration and termination using a preference-pruned auxiliary model and dual-indicator gating.
l02aE3Tujl.problem: Long Chain-of-Thought LLMs entangle exploration and termination in a single reasoning stream, causing excessive token usage and overthinking.
l02aE3Tujl.method: DeCoR applies preference-guided structured layer pruning to derive a smaller auxiliary explorer model that shares state with the base model. A dual-indicator gate monitoring predictive uncertainty and intermediate-answer consistency alternates between the auxiliary model for exploration and the base model for correction or termination.
l02aE3Tujl.key_idea: Alternates between a preference-pruned auxiliary explorer and the base model on a shared trajectory using an uncertainty-and-consistency gate.
l02aE3Tujl.evidence: Experiments across five reasoning benchmarks evaluate accuracy and CoT token reduction.

Iheig18Ge9.one_liner: Enables MLLMs to natively interleave continuous latent visual sketch tokens with text during autoregressive reasoning.
Iheig18Ge9.problem: Multimodal LLMs lack native visual imagination during reasoning and must rely on external toolkits or explicit image generation.
Iheig18Ge9.method: Sketch-in-Latents (SkiLa) extends autoregressive MLLMs to dynamically alternate between generating text tokens and continuous visual embeddings (latent sketch tokens). It is trained in two stages: SFT with latent visual semantics reconstruction, followed by RL with masked GRPO on the curated SkiLa-RL-4K dataset.
Iheig18Ge9.key_idea: Extends autoregressive MLLMs to generate continuous latent visual sketch tokens interleaved with text, trained via reconstruction SFT and masked GRPO.
Iheig18Ge9.evidence: Experiments on vision-centric tasks and multimodal benchmarks.

ZxwlQsl9Uj.one_liner: Rebalances LVLM visual attention using prefill token-importance and layer-activity scores plus a decoding-time visual dependency gate.
ZxwlQsl9Uj.problem: Uniform inference-time visual attention boosting in LVLMs reduces hallucinations but can degrade language generation quality when visual grounding is unnecessary.
ZxwlQsl9Uj.method: ViDRA scores visual token importance during prefill using representation stability and instruction relevance, sets layer-wise intervention strength from visual activity across Transformer layers, and uses a lightweight Visual Dependency Gate during decoding to boost visual attention only for visually dependent tokens.
ZxwlQsl9Uj.key_idea: Combines prefill token-importance and layer-activity scoring with a decoding-time Visual Dependency Gate to selectively boost visual attention.
ZxwlQsl9Uj.evidence: Experiments on visual hallucination benchmarks and general vision-language tasks.

qKCjf9nHV9.one_liner: Models non-conservative cellular microenvironment evolution using dual-scale unbalanced optimal transport and a direction-aware Graph Transformer.
qKCjf9nHV9.problem: Existing trajectory inference methods assume conservative dynamics or miss hierarchical organization and unknown temporal correspondences in evolving biological systems.
qKCjf9nHV9.method: NicheTime computes a dual-scale optimal transport coupling that aligns coarse structures then refines local correspondences while allowing variable mass flow. These transport plans supervise a direction-aware Graph Transformer flow-matching model integrated via neural ODEs to jointly generate system states and spatial configurations.
qKCjf9nHV9.key_idea: Pairs dual-scale mass-varying optimal transport coupling with a direction-aware Graph Transformer flow-matching ODE to model irreversible spatiotemporal evolution.
qKCjf9nHV9.evidence: Evaluations on three time-resolved spatial transcriptomics datasets covering embryonic development, neural development, and aging.

huryUurRTs.one_liner: Bilevel proxy LoRA adaptation trains implant backdoors to survive unseen downstream fine-tuning.
huryUurRTs.problem: Downstream fine-tuning can weaken pre-release LLM backdoors when attackers cannot access the downstream data, task, or adaptation procedure.
huryUurRTs.method: BiProxy separates a persistent implant LoRA from a disposable proxy LoRA that undergoes benign adaptation during each episode. A first-order bilevel update optimizes the fixed implant for trigger behavior after proxy adaptation and clean behavior otherwise, then discards the proxy.
huryUurRTs.key_idea: Optimize an implant LoRA against a resettable proxy adaptation trajectory so trigger behavior persists through unseen downstream updates.
huryUurRTs.evidence: Experiments cover two primary LLMs, two attack objectives, three downstream tasks, full-parameter and LoRA fine-tuning, benign utility, and proxy-removal ablations.
huryUurRTs.claimed_gains: BiProxy achieves post-adaptation attack success rates of 98.2%–100% under full-parameter fine-tuning and 93.2%–100% under LoRA fine-tuning in the default settings.

Haqle5zjeN.one_liner: Reliability-weighted pairwise relations reconcile into a system equilibrium used for simultaneous multi-system forecasts.
Haqle5zjeN.problem: Forecasting interacting systems requires modeling evolving relative relations rather than predicting each system in isolation.
Haqle5zjeN.method: RESE estimates pairwise relations from observed trajectories, weights them by reliability, and reconciles them into a system-level equilibrium state. It recovers individual forecasts by combining this equilibrium with a separately estimated aggregate.
Haqle5zjeN.key_idea: Reconcile reliability-weighted pairwise relations into one global equilibrium state from which individual system forecasts are recovered.
Haqle5zjeN.evidence: Experiments cover synthetic, exchange-rate, COVID-19, and multivariate datasets, standalone and combined forecasting, and tests of noise, missing observations, local shocks, and cross-system dependence.

l7ZgKRmG2R.one_liner: Execution-artifact schemas and AST checks gate geospatial code rewards on valid types and analytical operations.
l7ZgKRmG2R.problem: Executable geospatial programs can use incorrect sources, temporal ranges, coordinate systems, or workflows that unit tests and execution outcomes fail to detect.
l7ZgKRmG2R.method: GeoVR's HSVR extracts type-aware signatures from Google Earth Engine artifacts and checks analytical operations in the program AST. A hierarchical gate activates Schema and Method rewards only after correct task-level output type, while GRPO training uses structured execution errors to repair failed rollouts.
l7ZgKRmG2R.key_idea: Gate schema and method reward components on task-level execution and output-type correctness to prevent partial credit for invalid programs.
l7ZgKRmG2R.evidence: Evaluation on AutoGEEval++ covers Atomic, Combined, and Theme tasks with pass@1 comparisons against CodeGEEnius and a controlled Binary-RLVR baseline.
l7ZgKRmG2R.claimed_gains: On AutoGEEval++, GeoVR achieves pass@1 of 90.22%, 88.76%, and 67.82% on Atomic, Combined, and Theme tasks, outperforming CodeGEEnius by up to 6.38 points and Binary-RLVR by 3.73–10.35 points.

DUOifMInCP.one_liner: Label-free triggers, clustered buffers, and low-rank debugging deliver selective online teacher supervision to small models.
DUOifMInCP.problem: Deployed small language models degrade on unseen data, while conventional offline distillation cannot provide continuous teacher supervision after deployment.
DUOifMInCP.method: SAGE triggers distillation from teacher-student discrepancies without labels, organizes samples through streaming clustering and stability filtering, and searches low-rank updates in two stages for targeted injection. These modules support continual adaptation in streaming environments.
DUOifMInCP.key_idea: Select uncertain streaming inputs by teacher-student discrepancy, cluster them into knowledge regions, and inject targeted low-rank updates.
DUOifMInCP.evidence: The supplied abstract reports experiments on sample efficiency and adaptation accuracy but gives no datasets, baselines, or numerical results.

2QYrKm1aPJ.one_liner: A mental world model simulates evolving beliefs, uncertainties, and intentions for personalized e-commerce behavior.
2QYrKm1aPJ.problem: E-commerce simulators that directly predict actions from histories omit evolving mental states underlying personalization and realistic behavior.
2QYrKm1aPJ.method: ShopMind models how consumers interpret shopping information and how beliefs, uncertainties, and intentions evolve through interaction. Behavior-mental-state pairs synthesized by ShopMind train a Mental State Reconstruction model that infers latent states from observable behavior.
2QYrKm1aPJ.key_idea: Generate behavior from an evolving latent mental world and learn to reconstruct those mental states from observed actions.
2QYrKm1aPJ.evidence: The supplied abstract says experiments evaluate ShopMind but truncates before naming datasets, baselines, or results.

xjcnwIo9VA.one_liner: Symbolic polarity composition supplies local and global supervision for explicit and implicit affect reasoning.
xjcnwIo9VA.problem: Training only on final affect labels or overall rewards can miss errors in explicit expression, implicit attitude, and their relationship.
xjcnwIo9VA.method: PAIR uses two neural reasoning paths for explicit and implicit layers and symbolic rules that compose polarity judgments into affective stance. Supervised fine-tuning verifies trajectories, while reinforcement learning supplies local judgment rewards and global stance, intent, and emotion rewards.
xjcnwIo9VA.key_idea: Compose explicit and implicit polarity judgments symbolically so verification and rewards can target each layer and their consistency.
xjcnwIo9VA.evidence: CueBench experiments on Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-1.7B compare three-task average accuracy with DAPO and analyze structured supervision components.
xjcnwIo9VA.claimed_gains: On CueBench, PAIR achieves three-task average accuracies of 64.25% and 53.93% on Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-1.7B, outperforming DAPO by 5.88 and 3.37 percentage points, respectively.

aCtzPkszvi.one_liner: Reference-audio perturbations maximize contextual representation divergence to disrupt non-autoregressive speech synthesis trajectories.
aCtzPkszvi.problem: The adversarial robustness of reference-conditioned non-autoregressive text-to-speech models remains insufficiently studied.
aCtzPkszvi.method: The black-box attack perturbs reference audio to maximize contextual audio-representation divergence. Target-model measurements track attention redistribution and progressive separation of the generation trajectory.
aCtzPkszvi.key_idea: Maximize contextual representation divergence through small reference-audio perturbations to redistribute attention and separate synthesis trajectories.
aCtzPkszvi.evidence: Experiments cover five text-to-speech models at ε=0.01 and eight defenses: total variation and KL regularization, adversarial training, low-pass filtering, μ-law companding, randomized smoothing, Griffin-Lim, and score-based speech enhancement.
aCtzPkszvi.claimed_gains: The attack substantially reduces speaker fidelity across five text-to-speech models with ε=0.01 (SNR≈19dB) and persists against eight defenses.

ezMxDoekVz.one_liner: Computes partial-identification certificates and minimum identity disclosures needed to certify a near-optimal model under missing group links.
ezMxDoekVz.problem: When context identities such as hospital IDs are missing from evaluation records, model rankings can become nonidentifiable even when predictions and aggregate counts are public.
ezMxDoekVz.method: DeployRank solves exact partial-identification problems over all assignments consistent with public losses and group counts to certify when a model is within a target loss margin, determine the minimum number of disclosed links for two-candidate comparisons (with bounds for multiple candidates), and guide online querying via a one-step policy B1.
ezMxDoekVz.key_idea: Optimizing worst-case loss gaps over all unobserved context-group assignments consistent with public aggregates yields verifiable model-choice certificates and minimum disclosure counts.
ezMxDoekVz.evidence: Theoretical characterizations plus experiments on a 117-record source-record verification task and UCI Heart.
ezMxDoekVz.claimed_gains: In the 117-record verification task, the minimum certificate requires 4 links and online querying certifies after 15 requests; on UCI Heart, queries correct the initial choice on every tested path exceeding loss tolerance.

MlJPLfkIlD.one_liner: Contrastively aligns healthy structural MRI brain parcels to age-conditioned reference templates for zero-shot anomaly and disease scoring.
MlJPLfkIlD.problem: Learning anatomically grounded normative brain representations from healthy structural MRI that directly capture localized age-adjusted disease deviations remains challenging.
MlJPLfkIlD.method: BrainNorm is trained solely on healthy T1w sMRI scans via contrastive alignment to parcel-specific, age-conditioned healthy reference templates, forming a Semantic Atlas Latent (SAL) space that supports zero-shot disease-prior anomaly scoring and frozen linear probing.
MlJPLfkIlD.key_idea: Contrastive alignment of brain parcel embeddings to age-conditioned healthy reference templates constructs a Semantic Atlas Latent space where localized deviations directly support anomaly scoring.
MlJPLfkIlD.evidence: Trained and evaluated on ~66,000 T1w sMRI scans across downstream cohorts for age estimation, brain-age gap, parcel identification, and single-/multi-disease classification against nine fine-tuned baselines.
MlJPLfkIlD.claimed_gains: Across all supervised classification tasks, linear probing on BrainNorm's frozen embeddings outperforms nine baselines fine-tuned with end-to-end downstream supervision.

FJGLWNDv3J.one_liner: Analyzes compressed LoRA via bias-variance trade-offs and adds selected sparse residual coordinates in ProLoSA.
FJGLWNDv3J.problem: It is poorly understood when parameter-compressed LoRA outperforms standard LoRA and how to recover task-specific projection bias under a fixed parameter budget.
FJGLWNDv3J.method: The authors derive an energy-noise condition from a local quadratic decomposition and an exact sequence model characterizing compressed estimation bias versus variance, then propose ProLoSA, which pairs a compressed LoRA branch with selected sparse residual coordinates.
FJGLWNDv3J.key_idea: A local quadratic bias-variance analysis motivates combining a compressed shared LoRA branch with selected sparse residual coordinates when their recovery outweighs displaced compressed capacity.
FJGLWNDv3J.evidence: Theoretical analysis, controlled sequence and Transformer experiments, and downstream evaluations on language understanding, reasoning, instruction tuning, and vision.

aMz5GiLzrc.one_liner: Benchmarks context and knowledge hallucinations in large audio-language models using 12,000 open-ended pairs and a rubric-guided groundedness judge.
aMz5GiLzrc.problem: Existing audio hallucination benchmarks equate hallucination with incorrectness, failing to separate ungrounded claims from audio comprehension errors.
aMz5GiLzrc.method: MISHAP-Bench defines context hallucinations (ungrounded in audio) and knowledge hallucinations (unsupported by external facts) across 12,000 open-ended question-audio pairs, evaluated via a groundedness judge using human-guided reference rubrics.
aMz5GiLzrc.key_idea: Separating audio-ungrounded context hallucinations from externally unsupported knowledge hallucinations enables rubric-guided groundedness judging on open-ended audio-language responses.
aMz5GiLzrc.evidence: Evaluated ten large audio-language models and four adapted hallucination mitigation methods on 12,000 open-ended question-audio pairs.
aMz5GiLzrc.claimed_gains: Even Gemini 3.7 Flash reaches a hallucination rate of 36.5% on MISHAP-Bench.

6QFY5IrUnG.one_liner: Replaces trend decomposition in patch time-series forecasting with parallel patch-state encoding and explicit delta-dynamics modeling.
6QFY5IrUnG.problem: Trend-seasonal decomposition overlaps with local trend information already preserved in raw patches, yet similar local patch states can still hide distinct transition dynamics.
6QFY5IrUnG.method: PaDNet instantiates a state-dynamics forecasting paradigm with two parallel modules: Patch-State regularizes trajectory encoding to capture local temporal tendencies and structure, while Delta-Dynamics explicitly represents the direction and magnitude of adjacent changes and compares increments across steps.
6QFY5IrUnG.key_idea: Conditions time-series forecasts on both regularized Patch-State trajectory encodings and explicit adjacent-increment Delta-Dynamics representations instead of trend decomposition.

tymz0c9DV6.one_liner: Benchmarks earliest-fault localization in video-editing agent traces and improves judges by routing checkable state through deterministic tools.
tymz0c9DV6.problem: Pinpointing the earliest faulty step in long, tool-rich agent traces is difficult, and automatic LLM judges lag humans while over-attributing errors on clean traces.
tymz0c9DV6.method: The authors build AV-Fail, pairing a controlled fault-injection track across five fault types with 1,848 verified real multi-step video-editing agent traces. They introduce Trace-State Prompting, which routes checkable trace state through deterministic tools to assist automatic failure localization.
tymz0c9DV6.key_idea: Routes checkable intermediate agent-trace state through deterministic verification tools inside Trace-State Prompting to localize the earliest faulty step.
tymz0c9DV6.evidence: Evaluated across five judge models and a blind two-annotator human study on AV-Fail's controlled track and 1,848 real video-editing traces.
tymz0c9DV6.claimed_gains: Trace-State Prompting raises localization accuracy from 0.775 to 0.872; human agreement is Cohen's κ=0.63 versus κ=0.48 for the best single judge, with 1.00 on mechanical faults, 0.20 on cumulative-budget faults, and 0.35 false-positive rate on clean traces.

pUxM4Bm4al.one_liner: Fine-tunes a camera-controlled video diffusion model on synthetic interaction videos and multi-view data for interaction-preserving reshooting.
pUxM4Bm4al.problem: Synchronized multi-view datasets under-cover complex object interactions under diverse camera trajectories, hurting contact and dynamics fidelity during video reshooting.
pUxM4Bm4al.method: Rover distills interaction dynamics from a pretrained image-to-video model into ObjAlive, a filtered dataset of 13.5K interaction-rich videos covering contact, fluids, deformation, and articulation. It combines ObjAlive with synchronized multi-view and single-view real videos to fine-tune a video diffusion model conditioned on source videos and target-view warps.
pUxM4Bm4al.key_idea: Distills 13.5K filtered image-to-video interaction clips (ObjAlive) to fine-tune a warp-conditioned video diffusion model for viewpoint reshooting.
pUxM4Bm4al.evidence: Evaluated via blinded four-way human studies on held-out human-object interaction and robotic manipulation videos plus a step-matched ObjAlive ablation.
pUxM4Bm4al.claimed_gains: Rover receives 71.6% and 63.6% of interaction-fidelity votes in blinded four-way human evaluations on held-out human-object interaction and robotic manipulation videos, respectively.

k4dFvuGPXI.one_liner: Poisons hierarchical embodied agent memory by optimizing sparse scene-grounded visual cues that survive recursive consolidation.
k4dFvuGPXI.problem: Recursive consolidation in hierarchical embodied memories can preserve adversarial local visual cues in high-level summaries and misroute later retrieval.
k4dFvuGPXI.method: CueClimb operates during environment mapping using only local observations and auxiliary consolidation contexts without full-scene or query access. It constructs sparse, scene-grounded visual cues and searches for compact bundles whose semantic influence persists through recursive consolidation to redirect queries to attacker-chosen locations.
k4dFvuGPXI.key_idea: Searches for compact, scene-grounded local visual cue bundles that survive recursive memory consolidation to bias coarse-to-fine retrieval.
k4dFvuGPXI.evidence: Evaluated on 99 target-query cases across 23 HM3D scenes, including transfer tests across models, consolidation prompts, and hierarchical memory constructions.
k4dFvuGPXI.claimed_gains: CueClimb achieves a 46.5% attack success rate across 99 target-query cases in 23 HM3D scenes, compared with 28.3% for the strongest baseline.

Nw5SYz3nO4.one_liner: Disentangles fine-grained facial expression editing in diffusion models via symmetric joint training, intensity supervision, and contrastive learning.
Nw5SYz3nO4.problem: Intrinsic semantic overlap among facial expressions limits continuous intensity control and identity preservation in fine-grained expression editing.
Nw5SYz3nO4.method: The authors build the Flex Facial Expression (FFE) dataset with continuous affective annotations and FFE-Bench. They propose PixelSmile, a diffusion framework combining fully symmetric joint training, intensity supervision, and contrastive learning for linear expression control via textual latent interpolation.
Nw5SYz3nO4.key_idea: Uses fully symmetric joint diffusion training with intensity supervision and contrastive learning to enable linear textual-latent interpolation of facial expressions.
Nw5SYz3nO4.evidence: Evaluated on the newly constructed FFE dataset and FFE-Bench measuring structural confusion, editing accuracy, linear controllability, and identity preservation.

pXDkck7KKC.one_liner: Optimizes dense image captioning via reinforcement learning with quantitative rewards from sampled completeness and faithfulness queries.
pXDkck7KKC.problem: Open-ended image captioning lacks verifiable rewards, making reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards difficult to apply directly.
pXDkck7KKC.method: DQ-RL constructs a pool of completeness queries and faithfulness queries, performs unified sampling over them to score generated caption sub-capabilities, and uses these quantitative scores as RL rewards. The authors also build the DQ-CAP-40k training dataset and the DQ-Bench evaluation benchmark.
pXDkck7KKC.key_idea: Scores generated captions against unified samples of completeness and faithfulness queries to supply quantitative RL rewards for dense captioning.
pXDkck7KKC.evidence: Evaluates a 4B DQ-RL model trained on DQ-CAP-40k under the PRISM framework and on DQ-Bench.
pXDkck7KKC.claimed_gains: The 4B DQ-RL model achieves a 1.4% average improvement over baselines under PRISM and matches Qwen3.5-27B at 63.1%.

pHFRKl5vsA.one_liner: Benchmarks bimanual fabric manipulation with a contact-driven Newton deformable simulator, six tasks, and 10,000 assets.
pHFRKl5vsA.problem: Standardized robot manipulation benchmarks focus on rigid objects and rely on artificial attachment rather than realistic contact forces for deformable fabrics.
pHFRKl5vsA.method: FabricBench introduces six bimanual fabric tasks spanning garments, silk, and bags with 10,000 simulation assets and controlled configuration and appearance generalization tests. Built on Newton, its simulator redesigns cloth-rigid contact and bidirectional force coupling for grasping, holding, and releasing without artificial attachment.
pHFRKl5vsA.key_idea: Uses redesigned cloth-rigid contact and bidirectional force coupling in Newton to benchmark bimanual fabric policies without artificial grasping attachments.
pHFRKl5vsA.evidence: Evaluates solver grasp-hold-release over 45 trials, six policies (including VLA and world-action models) in simulation, and zero-shot real-robot deployment of π0.5.
pHFRKl5vsA.claimed_gains: The simulator succeeds in all 45 grasp-hold-release trials versus 0 for baselines; the best policy averages 77% success, no policy exceeds 36% on T-shirt folding, and success drops to 6–14% under the most deformed initial T-shirts.

8EmiXfV800.one_liner: Benchmarks deep-search agents across escalating web-poisoning levels using a Search-Scrape interface and five-state trajectory rubric.
8EmiXfV800.problem: Existing benchmarks check whether search agents retrieve or endorse poisoned content, but not how agents verify or recover from poisoned web evidence during search.
8EmiXfV800.method: HAE-GEO holds a fabricated brand and false claim fixed across three presentation levels—direct assertion, contextual camouflage, and multi-page corroboration—inside a corpus of 72,039 clean and 770 poisoned pages per level. Agents act through a Search-Scrape interface, and trajectories are mapped to five states and scored on a six-dimensional rubric.
8EmiXfV800.key_idea: Escalates identical false claims from direct assertion to multi-page corroboration inside a Search-Scrape corpus while scoring five trajectory states.
8EmiXfV800.evidence: Evaluates ten deep-search agents on 72,039 clean and 770 poisoned pages per level, including matched page-type/length controls and defense prompting.

RXiElS9wVM.one_liner: Diagnoses graph-enhanced multi-agent LLM systems via controlled component interventions across 29 datasets and 400 complex tasks.
RXiElS9wVM.problem: Existing multi-agent benchmarks report only final task scores and do not isolate how graph topologies handle information integration, error propagation, or recovery.
RXiElS9wVM.method: OpenMAS-GCom provides a controlled intervention framework decomposing graph-enhanced multi-agent systems into collaboration units, communication links, shared intermediate state, and execution strategies under fixed tasks and budgets. It also introduces G-MAS-Complex with 400 multi-document integration and conflict-resolution tasks.
RXiElS9wVM.key_idea: Intervenes independently on collaboration units, communication links, shared state, and execution strategies under fixed models and budgets to diagnose G-MAS.
RXiElS9wVM.evidence: Covers 29 datasets across six domains, including 400 G-MAS-Complex tasks, evaluating 17 representative G-MAS configurations.

sN2AiyLkXQ.one_liner: Benchmarks multi-view 3D generative verification decisions, explanations, and perturbation consistency across 10 tasks.
sN2AiyLkXQ.problem: Verifying whether generated 3D assets satisfy explicit requirements and explaining contradictions across multiple views remains unreliable for MLLMs.
sN2AiyLkXQ.method: The authors introduce 3DVerifierBench, a 10-task benchmark assessing whether verifiers correctly accept or reject 3D candidates, explain contradicting facts, and stay consistent under controlled requirement or candidate edits, alongside a scalable 3D verification data pipeline.
sN2AiyLkXQ.key_idea: Tests 3D verification decisions, contradiction explanations, and consistency under controlled requirement or candidate changes across multi-view observations.
sN2AiyLkXQ.evidence: Evaluates MLLMs including GPT-6 Astra against a human study across 10 tasks in 3DVerifierBench and fine-grained factual categories.
sN2AiyLkXQ.claimed_gains: A human study reveals a 21.6 percentage-point gap between humans and the strongest tested model, GPT-6 Astra.

zRSPtifHOP.one_liner: Detects structural tabular anomalies by integrating multi-scale deviations along causally organized Matryoshka representation trajectories.
zRSPtifHOP.problem: Single fixed latent representations dilute localized dependency violations in high-dimensional tabular data where individual features look normal.
zRSPtifHOP.method: NestedAno learns nested Matryoshka-style representations progressively organized with topologically aligned causal reconstruction objectives. At inference, it measures local deviation at each nested scale to form an anomaly trajectory and integrates its deviation from normal references as the anomaly score.
zRSPtifHOP.key_idea: Organizes nested Matryoshka representations with causal reconstruction objectives and integrates per-scale deviations into a trajectory-based anomaly score.
zRSPtifHOP.evidence: Evaluated across 30 continuous and mixed-type tabular datasets against 17 representative anomaly-detection baselines.
zRSPtifHOP.claimed_gains: Achieves the highest average AUC-ROC among 17 representative baselines across 30 continuous and mixed-type datasets (exact numbers not stated).

pdivZC83Kj.one_liner: Analyzes metastable retrieval and multi-channel Kramers centroid hopping in continuous log-sum-ReLU dense associative memory.
pdivZC83Kj.problem: The finite-temperature stability and escape dynamics of retrieval states in continuous log-sum-ReLU dense associative memory were not characterized across load and temperature.
pdivZC83Kj.method: The authors analyze the log-sum-ReLU energy on the N-sphere across load α and temperature T, partitioning retrieval into stable, metastable, and merged-centroid regimes. They model escape from the metastable basin into two-pattern centroids as a multi-channel Kramers process over entropic barriers and derive the disorder-averaged escape rate.
pdivZC83Kj.key_idea: Models retrieval escape in log-sum-ReLU associative memory as a multi-channel Kramers process over entropic barriers whose rate decays exponentially with dimension N.
pdivZC83Kj.evidence: Supported by statistical-mechanics analysis and Monte Carlo simulations across load and temperature ranges.

NWmbeQDCvc.one_liner: Predicts word-level AI editing indicators and conditional edit intensity from aligned source-edited training pairs.
NWmbeQDCvc.problem: Conventional AI-text detectors classify whole documents as human or AI, or output a single document score, without localizing edited words or separating edit scope from intensity.
NWmbeQDCvc.method: MixDetect aligns source-edited text pairs during training to build word-level supervision and trains a model that predicts both whether each word was AI-edited and, conditionally, how substantial the edit is. At inference, it operates on the input text alone and can also aggregate predictions for document-level classification.
NWmbeQDCvc.key_idea: Separately predicts per-word edit probability and conditional edit intensity trained on aligned source-edited pairs, requiring only raw text at inference.
NWmbeQDCvc.evidence: Evaluated on word-level localization, editing-intensity sensitivity, human/AI edit sequences, and binary/ternary text classification under domain and generator shifts.

53GnOvRv4K.one_liner: Jointly admits and places agentic LLM sessions across GPU clusters using a tool-readiness value interface and dynamic program.
53GnOvRv4K.problem: Existing LLM serving schedulers ignore external tool-return readiness and rely on heuristics for GPU admission and placement in alternating GPU-inference/CPU-tool agent workloads.
53GnOvRv4K.method: TAO scores waiting agentic sessions via a value interface combining near-term tool readiness, time-decayed node-specific cache credit, and token footprint. A dynamic program then jointly selects and places sessions onto GPUs under capacity constraints.
53GnOvRv4K.key_idea: Scores waiting sessions by tool-return readiness, time-decayed cache credit, and token footprint, then solves GPU admission and placement via dynamic programming.
53GnOvRv4K.evidence: Evaluated across 12 model-workload-concurrency settings against existing serving baselines.
53GnOvRv4K.claimed_gains: Across 12 settings, TAO reduces latency by up to 26.8%, reduces mean TTFT by up to 36.3%, and increases decode throughput by up to 29.5% relative to the best baseline per metric.

6gQ9WRaCo0.one_liner: Formalizes optimizer-aware online data selection and proves diagonal-adaptive preconditioners avoid discriminability collapse.
6gQ9WRaCo0.problem: Online batch data selection for LLM pretraining typically ignores how the optimizer preconditions raw gradients before updating model parameters.
6gQ9WRaCo0.method: OptiSelect formalizes optimizer-aware data selection via a selection-gain principle linking selection benefit to the discriminability of optimizer-induced utility scores and deriving the optimal candidate oversampling ratio. The theory compares sign-based and polar-tangential preconditioners (Lion, Muon) against diagonal-adaptive ones (AdamW, Sophia).
6gQ9WRaCo0.key_idea: Scores candidate training examples under the optimizer's preconditioning geometry and shows diagonal-adaptive scoring avoids the discriminability collapse of sign or polar-tangential updates.
6gQ9WRaCo0.evidence: Supported by theoretical discriminability bounds and LLM pretraining experiments on 124M and 720M models, including under data rephrasing.

M6mvM9VAIh.one_liner: Characterizes exact approximation guarantees and query-budget lower bounds for cardinality-constrained submodular maximization using distorted marginal-gain surrogates.
M6mvM9VAIh.problem: Prior error bounds on surrogate function values for submodular maximization yield pessimistic impossibility results with no constant-factor polynomial-query guarantee.
M6mvM9VAIh.method: Measuring surrogate error as a multiplicative distortion η on marginal gains, the paper analyzes deterministic surrogate-only algorithms and determines three exact prices: the information price 1/η, the exact predictive-greedy guarantee ρ_K(η), and the budget price showing predictive greedy is optimal under nK queries for n ≥ K^4.
M6mvM9VAIh.key_idea: Parameterized by multiplicative marginal-gain distortion η, proves exact information, predictive-greedy, and nK-query budget approximation limits for surrogate submodular maximization.
M6mvM9VAIh.evidence: Theoretical upper and lower bounds for deterministic surrogate-only algorithms and predictive greedy under cardinality constraint K.
M6mvM9VAIh.claimed_gains: Establishes exact information price 1/η and predictive-greedy guarantee ρ_K(η) tending to 1 - e^(-1/η), optimal among deterministic nK-query algorithms for n ≥ K^4.

F2FsHCBv4V.one_liner: Builds a discrete latent world model with dual reconstructive/feature-aligned latents and one-step flow-matching dynamics prediction.
F2FsHCBv4V.problem: One-step discrete world models ignore inter-token dependencies via factorized sampling (while multi-step refinement is slow), and encoders trade off visual detail against task-relevant abstraction.
F2FsHCBv4V.method: FLORA pairs a Dual-latent Representation combining a stochastic reconstructive latent with an auxiliary feature-aligned latent, and predicts next latents using a Denoising Latent Predictor trained with continuous flow matching and shortcut forcing for single-step dependency-aware imagination.
F2FsHCBv4V.key_idea: Combines dual reconstructive and feature-aligned discrete latents with a one-step continuous flow-matching predictor trained via shortcut forcing to capture inter-token dependencies.
F2FsHCBv4V.evidence: Evaluated on Atari 100k and the DeepMind Control Suite.
